definition_zh: 贵族；贵族出身的人；（比喻）最佳者、翘楚
definition_en: a member of the highest social class, especially one born into nobility
core_image: 世袭纹章下坐于高位的世家子弟
scene: 宴会厅里烛光摇曳，宾客个个佩着家传徽章。 The old aristocrat greeted every guest with courtly grace.
sceneCN: 这里 aristocrat 是「贵族」（第 1 个义项：世袭上层阶级成员）；句意是老贵族以典雅的仪态向每位宾客致意。

（某领域）最优秀者；翘楚

derivatives.zh: aristocrat 加形容词后缀 -ic，义为「贵族的；气派高雅的」
aristocrat 的抽象名词，义为「贵族阶层；贵族政体」

senses.title: A member of the nobility
senses.titleCN: 贵族；世袭上层阶级成员
senses.definition: a person born into the highest hereditary social class, holding rank or titles
senses.definitionCN: 出身于最高世袭社会阶层、拥有爵位或头衔的人
senses.example: Hundreds of aristocrats fled France during the Revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 大革命期间数百名贵族逃离法国。
senses.why: The Greek root aristo- means best, and the best-born were the nobles.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 aristo- 意为「最好的」，出身最显赫者即贵族。

senses.title: A person of aristocratic manner
senses.definition: anyone whose style, manners or tastes suggest the refined elegance of the nobility
senses.definitionCN: 举止品味带有贵族式优雅气派的人，不论出身
senses.example: Though poor, she carried herself like an aristocrat.
senses.exampleCN: 她虽穷，举手投足却像位贵族。
senses.why: The manner is detached from the class and taken as a quality in itself.
senses.whyCN: 气派脱离阶级，本身成为可独立拥有的品质。

senses.title: The finest of its kind
senses.definition: something regarded as the best or most distinguished of its class
senses.definitionCN: 被视为同类中最优秀、最出众的事物
senses.example: This saffron is the aristocrat of all spices.
senses.exampleCN: 这种藏红花是香料中的极品。
senses.why: Aristo- literally means best, so the word returns to its root when ranking things.
senses.whyCN: aristo- 本义即「最好」，比喻义实际上是向词根的回归。

intro.en: Aristocrat comes from Greek aristokrates, a person of the best rule, from aristos and kratos.
intro.cn: aristocrat 源自希腊语 aristokrates，由 aristos（最好的）与 kratos（权力）构成。

items.en: Roots *h2er- (fit together) and *kratos-related stems are reconstructed for best and power.
items.cn: 「最好」与「权力」两词根被分别重构为 *h2er- 及 kratos 相关词干（重构形式）。

items.en: Aristos meant best; kratos meant power or rule; aristokrates named one of the best ruling class.
items.cn: 希腊语 aristos 意为「最好的」，kratos 意为「权力」，aristokrates 指最优统治阶层的一员。

items.en: Aristokratia named government by the best citizens, first a political, not a birth, category.
items.cn: aristokratia 本指「贤良治国」，最初按德才而非血统划分。

items.en: French aristocrate spread in the 18th century, often as a hostile label before the Revolution.
items.cn: 法语 aristocrate 在 18 世纪流行，大革命前常作贬斥标签。

items.en: English borrowed aristocrat in the 1790s in the French political sense.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪 90 年代借入 aristocrat，取其法国政治语境义。

items.en: Today it names nobles by birth and, figuratively, the finest of any class of things.
items.cn: 现代英语既指出身贵族，也比喻各类事物中的极品。

note.en: The family splits into a person (aristocrat), a class (aristocracy) and a style (aristocratic).
note.cn: 词族分工：指人的 aristocrat、指阶层的 aristocracy、指风格的 aristocratic。

normal.cn: aristos 意为「最好」，crat 意为「权力」：居上而治的「最优者」。

normal.en: The -crat family: autocrat, bureaucrat, technocrat.

normal.en: Figuratively, the aristocrat of tea means the finest tea.

abstract.en: Picture a man with a gold-topped cane inspecting a vineyard he never worked.

abstract.en: Hear the slow, unhurried voice that assumes it will be obeyed.

examples.en: The young aristocrat spent his inheritance on travel and books.

examples.en: She married an impoverished aristocrat with a grand name.

examples.en: Connoisseurs rank this vintage as the aristocrat of Burgundies.

definition_zh: 洋流；海洋中沿固定方向持续流动的水体
definition_en: a continuous, directed flow of seawater, set in motion by winds, by differences in temperature and salinity, or by tides
core_image: 海面或深海里藏着一条看不见的河，两岸都是海水，水却固执地朝同一侧走
scene: 海洋课上，老师指着海图上从热带伸向高纬的蓝色带子说， An ocean current carries warm water far from the equator.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean current 指「海洋中沿固定方向持续流动的水体」（第 1 个义项：泛指洋流）；句意为：一股洋流把暖水从赤道带向远方。

pos.zh: 洋流；海洋中沿固定方向持续流动的水体

derivatives.zh: 西边界流（沿大洋西缘向极地流动的强而窄的洋流）
边界流；沿海岸或海盆边缘流动的洋流
风生流；由盛行风推动的表层洋流
海流计；测量流速与流向的仪器
温盐流；由温度与盐度差异驱动的深层水流

senses.title: Seawater that keeps to one direction
senses.titleCN: 沿固定方向持续流动的海水
senses.definition: a continuous, directed movement of seawater that persists over long distances
senses.definitionCN: 在长距离上持续保持同一方向的海水流动
senses.example: An ocean current can be as steady as a river in its channel.
senses.exampleCN: 一股洋流可以像河道里的河水一样稳定。
senses.why: the phrase simply names the sea's version of a river: water that runs in a channel of its own, marked out by heat, salt and wind rather than by banks.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只是给海里那条「河」命名：水在自己的通道里奔跑，通道由热、盐与风划定，而不是由河岸划定。

senses.title: The wind-driven surface flow
senses.definition: the current in the upper ocean, set in motion and shaped by the prevailing winds
senses.definitionCN: 上层海洋中由盛行风驱动并塑造的水流
senses.example: The trade winds drive a surface ocean current westward along the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 信风驱动表层洋流沿赤道向西流动。
senses.why: wind drags the top of the sea the way it drags a cloth, so the uppermost layer becomes the current that pulls the rest along.
senses.whyCN: 风拖动海面，像拖动一块布，于是最上面那层水成了拖动其余水体的洋流。

senses.title: The density-driven deep flow
senses.definition: the slow current of cold, dense water in the deep ocean, driven by differences in temperature and salt
senses.definitionCN: 深海中由温度与盐分差异驱动的寒冷高密度水的缓慢流动
senses.example: A deep ocean current carries Antarctic water north along the sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一股深层洋流沿海底把南极的水向北输送。
senses.why: cold and salty water is heavy, so it sinks and pushes along the bottom; gravity, not wind, is the engine here.
senses.whyCN: 又冷又咸的水更重，于是下沉并沿底部推进；这里的动力是重力，不是风。

senses.title: The narrow current at a coast
senses.titleCN: 沿海岸流动的窄而急的水流
senses.definition: a strong, narrow current that runs along the edge of a continent, such as the Gulf Stream or the Kuroshio
senses.definitionCN: 沿大陆边缘流动的强劲窄流，如墨西哥湾流或黑潮
senses.example: This boundary ocean current keeps the harbour ice-free in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这股边界洋流使港口在冬季不结冰。
senses.why: water piled against a coast has only the edge to escape along, so it narrows and speeds up, which is why such currents are the fastest in the sea.
senses.whyCN: 被堆到岸边的水只能沿边缘找出路，于是变窄、加速，这正是这类洋流成为海中流速最快者的原因。

senses.title: The currents along the equator
senses.definition: the eastward and westward currents that run parallel to the equator, driven by the trade winds
senses.definitionCN: 与赤道平行、由信风驱动的向东与向西水流
senses.example: Equatorial ocean currents shift eastward when the trade winds relax.
senses.exampleCN: 信风减弱时，赤道洋流向东移动。
senses.why: the equator is where the winds are steadiest, so the currents there become the most regular lanes in the ocean.
senses.whyCN: 赤道一带风最稳定，因此那里的洋流成了海洋中最规律的通道。

senses.title: The current that follows the tide
senses.definition: the horizontal movement of water produced by the rise and fall of the tide, reversing direction through the day
senses.definitionCN: 由潮汐涨落引起的水平水流，一天之内改变方向
senses.example: Where the tide runs hard, the ocean current reverses with it.
senses.exampleCN: 在潮水强劲处，洋流也随之反向。
senses.why: the tide does not only lift the surface; it also drags water sideways, and that horizontal part is read as a current.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐并不只是抬高水面，它还会横向拖动海水，而这一横向部分就被看作水流。

senses.title: The current that follows a shore
senses.definition: a current that runs parallel to a shoreline, often carrying sediment and larvae along the coast
senses.definitionCN: 与海岸线平行流动的水流，常沿岸输送泥沙与幼体
senses.example: A coastal ocean current moves sand southward along the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 一股沿岸洋流沿海滩把沙向南搬运。
senses.why: waves breaking at an angle push water along the shore, so the beach itself generates a current that follows its own line.
senses.whyCN: 斜向破碎的波浪把水沿岸推挤，海滩因而生成一股沿着自身轮廓流动的水流。

senses.title: The current as a carrier of heat
senses.definition: a current regarded as a conveyor that moves heat, salt and carbon between latitudes and basins
senses.definitionCN: 被视作在纬度与海盆之间输送热量、盐分与碳的水流
senses.example: The ocean current releases its heat to the air over the northern Atlantic.
senses.exampleCN: 这股洋流把热量释放给北大西洋上空的空气。
senses.why: once the flow is mapped, it stops being only water and becomes a carrier: what it transports matters more than what it is.
senses.whyCN: 水流一旦被测绘成图，它就不只是水，而成为载体：它输送什么，比它本身是什么更重要。

senses.title: The current as a route
senses.definition: a current used as a path by drifting organisms, ships or floating debris
senses.definitionCN: 被漂流生物、船只或漂浮物当作路径使用的水流
senses.example: Larvae travel on the ocean current from the reef to the nursery ground.
senses.exampleCN: 幼体随这股洋流从珊瑚礁前往育幼场。
senses.why: anything that floats and cannot swim has no choice of direction, so the current becomes its road.
senses.whyCN: 任何漂浮且不会游动的东西都无法选择方向，于是洋流就成了它的路。

intro.en: Ocean current is a compound of two borrowed words: ocean from Greek Okeanos by way of Latin and Old French, current from Latin currere 'to run'. The fixed phrase belongs to the language of navigation and nineteenth-century oceanography. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean current 由两个外来词复合而成：ocean 出自希腊 Okeanos，经拉丁语与古法语传来；current 出自拉丁 currere「跑」。这一固定短语属于航海语言与 19 世纪海洋学写作。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek Okeanos, the river thought to encircle the world, became Latin Oceanus and Old French occean, and named the great salt water in English.
items.cn: 希腊 Okeanos 是古人想象中环绕世界的大河，后为拉丁 Oceanus 与古法语 occean，在英语中指巨大的咸水体。

items.en: Latin currens, current- 'running' gave Old French corant and English current, first of running water and later of moving air and charge.
items.cn: 拉丁 currens, current-「跑着的」产生古法语 corant 与英语 current，先指流动的水，后指流动的空气与电荷。

items.en: By the sixteenth century sailors were recording currents at sea, and the plain noun current was enough; the compound was not yet fixed.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，水手已在记录海上的水流，单用名词 current 就够；复合短语尚未固定。

items.en: When wind and current charts were published for navigators in the nineteenth century, ocean current settled as the standard term of the new science of the sea.
items.cn: 19 世纪为航海者刊行风与海流图时，ocean current 固定下来，成为新兴海洋科学的标准术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century physical oceanography classified ocean currents by their driver and position: surface, deep, boundary, equatorial, coastal and tidal.
items.cn: 20 世纪的物理海洋学按驱动因素与位置把洋流分类：表层、深层、边界、赤道、沿岸与潮流。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the compound only, not the roots): the exact first use of the phrase is not fixed, and its spread is generally associated with nineteenth-century chart-making rather than with a single author; both component roots are well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅就复合短语的首见年代，不涉及词根）：该短语最早的用例没有确切年份，其流行一般认为是随 19 世纪制图而扩散，而非出自某位作者；两个构词成分的词根文献确凿。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the same two words or near neighbours of the compound; group two holds other names for moving water that differ in scale or cause.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个词构成、或与该短语相邻的说法；第二组是其他指流动之水的名称，规模或成因不同。

entries.definition: the single word covers water, air and electricity; only the compound keeps the meaning inside the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 单独一个词可指水、空气与电；只有复合短语把意义限定在海里。

entries.definition: a less technical variant using sea instead of ocean; it is correct but occurs far less often in oceanography.
entries.definitionCN: 用 sea 代替 ocean 的不太技术的变体；说法正确，但在海洋学文献中远不常见。

entries.definition: a current produced by the tide alone; it is a kind of ocean current but is named for its cause rather than its place.
entries.definitionCN: 仅由潮汐产生的水流；它属于洋流的一种，但按成因而非按地点命名。

entries.definition: the whole system of flows, including wind-driven and density-driven parts; a current is one strand within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个流动系统，包括风驱动与密度驱动的部分；洋流只是其中一股。

entries.definition: in oceanography a stream is a narrow, well-defined current, as in the Florida Stream; the scale is smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 在海洋学中指狭窄而边界清楚的水流，如佛罗里达流；尺度更小。

entries.definition: the general movement of surface water under wind; it stresses displacement rather than a fixed channel.
entries.definitionCN: 表层水在风下的整体移动；强调位移，而不强调固定通道。

entries.definition: a large closed loop formed by several currents around a basin; it is the loop, not one current in it.
entries.definitionCN: 由数股洋流绕海盆形成的大型闭合环路；它指整个环路，而非其中一股洋流。

entries.definition: a swirl of water that has broken away from the main flow; it spins instead of travelling in one direction.
entries.definitionCN: 脱离主流的旋转水团；它打转，而不是朝一个方向长途行进。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A current is a river inside the sea: ocean names the water, current names the running.
normal.cn: 洋流是海里的一条河：ocean 命名水域，current 命名奔跑。

normal.en: The phrase is a compound noun, so its plural is ocean currents.
normal.cn: 这个短语是复合名词，复数为 ocean currents。

normal.en: Its classes follow the driver: wind at the surface, density in the deep, tide at the coast.
normal.cn: 它的分类跟着驱动因素走：表层靠风，深层靠密度，沿岸靠潮。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: surface ocean current, deep ocean current, warm ocean current, ocean current system.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：表层洋流、深层洋流、暖洋流、洋流系统。

normal.en: The single word current also covers air and electricity; only the compound keeps it in the sea.
normal.cn: 单用的 current 也指空气与电；只有这个复合短语把它留在海里。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon laid on the water and followed for thousands of kilometres.
abstract.cn: 想象一条铺在水上的缎带，被追随了数千公里。

abstract.en: Picture a bottle thrown into the sea arriving on a beach it never chose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被扔进海里的瓶子，抵达一片它从未选择的沙滩。

abstract.en: Picture a warm room built into cold water and moving slowly north.
abstract.cn: 想象一间造在冷水里的暖房，正缓慢向北移动。

examples.en: The Gulf Stream is the best-known warm ocean current in the Atlantic.
examples.cn: 墨西哥湾流是大西洋中最著名的暖洋流。

examples.en: Deep ocean currents move water that has not seen the surface for centuries.
examples.cn: 深层洋流搬运着数百年未见过表层的水。

examples.en: Sailors once relied on an ocean current to shorten a crossing.
examples.cn: 水手曾依靠洋流来缩短航程。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词＋谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧申＋卡润特」——大洋里那股一直「跑」的水 → 洋流

root: 复合短语：ocean（希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean）+ current（拉丁 currere「跑」的现在分词 currens, current- → 古法语 corant）；在海洋学写作中固化为「洋流」；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，currere 的印欧来源一般重构为 *kers-「跑」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one stream: the general flow, then the layer the wind drives, the deep water that density drives, the fast edge currents, the equatorial lanes, the tidal and coastal versions, and finally the current as a carrier of heat and as a road for drifters.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一股水流：先是一般的洋流，然后是风驱动的表层、密度驱动的深层、沿岸的急流、赤道的通道、潮汐与沿岸的变体，最后是作为热量载体与漂流者通道的洋流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river inside the sea, with water for both banks and a direction of its own.
core.cn: 核心意象：海里的一条河，两岸都是水，而它有自己坚定的方向。

branches.en: THE FLOW ITSELF: first the general stream, then the upper layer that the wind drags with it.
branches.cn: 流动本身：先是一般的洋流，然后是被风拖动的最上层。

branches.en: THE DEEP AND THE EDGE: heavy water sinks and runs along the bottom, while water piled at a coast races along it.
branches.cn: 深处与边缘：重水下沉并沿底部奔跑，而被堆到岸边的水则沿岸疾走。

branches.en: LATITUDE AND CLOCK: the steadiest lanes follow the equator, and the most regular reversals follow the tide.
branches.cn: 纬度与时钟：最稳定的通道沿赤道，最规律的往复随潮汐。

branches.en: ALONG THE SHORE: sediment and larvae travel parallel to the beach on a current of its own.
branches.cn: 沿岸：泥沙与幼体顺着一股自成的沿岸流，与海滩平行地移动。

branches.en: WHAT IT CARRIES: the current as a conveyor of heat and salt, and as a road for anything that drifts.
branches.cn: 它载着什么：洋流既是热与盐的输送带，也是任何漂流之物的路。

intro.en: Ocean current is a two-word technical compound; its parts come from Greek and Latin, and the same pieces recur in the vocabulary of the sea.
intro.cn: ocean current 是双词技术复合语；两部分分别来自希腊语与拉丁语，同样的构件在海洋词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus supplies ocean and its relatives, while Latin currere supplies current and the whole family of course and cursor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Oceanus 提供 ocean 及其同族词，拉丁 currere 则提供 current 以及 course、cursor 整族词。

definition_zh: 君主的；君主制的；拥护君主制的；君主般专断的；以一人为顶点的
definition_en: relating to a monarch or to monarchy; favouring royal rule; or resembling a monarch in manner and structure
core_image: 一份组织图的最上方只画着一个王冠，下面的线全部汇到这一点
scene: 会议室的白板上画着一张架构图，最上方只有一个圆圈，底下所有箭头都汇向它。 The board's monarchic structure gave one chair the final word on every budget.
sceneCN: 这里 monarchic 指「以一人为顶点、像君主制那样组织的」（第 5 个义项：单一首脑结构）；句意为董事会的君主式结构让一把椅子对每项预算拥有最终决定权。可辨识物件：白板、架构图、圆圈、箭头、椅子。

pos.zh: 君主的；君主制的；拥护君主制的；专断的

derivatives.zh: monarchic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 以君主方式地
monarchic 的 -ical 变体，语义相同而语体更正式
monarch + -ism（主义后缀）→ 君主主义，由形容词转为政治主张
monarch + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 君主主义者
monarch + -y（状态后缀）→ 君主制，由属性转回制度
希腊 monarkhes 经拉丁 → 君主，为整个词族的人称基础

senses.title: Relating to a monarch
senses.definition: belonging to the person of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 属于国王、女王或皇帝本人的
senses.example: The monarchic title passed to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 君主称号传给了长子。
senses.why: The suffix -ic makes a relational adjective, so the word simply means 'of a monarch' at its base.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此这个词最基本的意思就是「君主的」。

senses.title: Relating to monarchy as a system
senses.titleCN: 与君主制这一制度相关的
senses.definition: describing the institutions and practices of rule by a hereditary head of state
senses.definitionCN: 描述由世袭元首统治的制度与实践
senses.example: Monarchic government survived in a few small states.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制政府在少数小国中留存下来。
senses.why: Because the adjective can modify 'government' or 'system', it extends from the person to the whole arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个形容词可修饰「政府」或「体系」，便从人扩展到整套安排。

senses.title: Favouring royal rule
senses.definition: supporting the restoration or preservation of a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 支持恢复或保留君主制
senses.example: The monarchic party opposed the referendum.
senses.exampleCN: 拥护君主制的政党反对这次公投。
senses.why: A political adjective often names a stance rather than a fact, so monarchic can mean 'on the side of the crown'.
senses.whyCN: 政治形容词常命名立场而非事实，因此 monarchic 可指「站在王冠一边」。

senses.title: Characteristic of a monarch's manner
senses.definition: showing the assurance, distance or dignity associated with a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 表现出与统治者相关的笃定、距离感或威仪
senses.example: He spoke with a monarchic assurance that ended debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着君主般的笃定说话，终止了辩论。
senses.why: The adjective moves from office to temperament, so an unelected chair can sound monarchic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从职位移到性情，因此一位非经选举的主席也能显得像君主。

senses.title: Structured with one person at the top
senses.definition: organised so that a single person holds final authority over everyone else
senses.definitionCN: 组织方式使一人对其余所有人握有最终权威
senses.example: The board's monarchic structure gave one chair the final word on every budget.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会的君主式结构让一把椅子对每项预算拥有最终决定权。
senses.why: The political shape is applied to an organisation, where one signature can override a whole committee.
senses.whyCN: 政治形态被套用到组织上，一个签名便可压倒整个委员会。

senses.title: Of a state with a crowned head
senses.definition: describing a country whose head of state holds a royal title
senses.definitionCN: 描述元首拥有王室称号的国家
senses.example: Monarchic states dominated the peninsula for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制国家曾支配这个半岛数百年。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the state as well as to the office, since a country can be described by its constitutional form.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也修饰国家，因为一国可由其宪制形式来描述。

senses.title: Domineering in personal habit
senses.definition: acting as though one's word cannot be questioned, like an absolute ruler
senses.definitionCN: 行事仿佛自己的话不容置疑，像绝对统治者
senses.example: Her monarchic habits alienated the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她专断的作风让员工疏远了她。
senses.why: The critical use turns the adjective from description into reproach: a small tyrant in an office.
senses.whyCN: 批评性用法把这个形容词从描述变为责备：办公室里的一个小暴君。

senses.title: Of a particular royal era
senses.definition: describing a historical period governed by a monarch or a royal regime
senses.definitionCN: 描述由君主或王室政权统治的历史时期
senses.example: Monarchic France collapsed in the revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制的法国在大革命中崩溃。
senses.why: Historians use the adjective to label a regime and its era, just as they use dynastic for a ruling house.
senses.whyCN: 史家用这个形容词标记政权及其时代，正如用 dynastic 标记统治家族。

intro.en: Monarchic is the Greek adjective monarkhikos, built on monarkhes 'sole ruler' with the suffix -ikos, which Latin reshaped as -icus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monarchic 是希腊形容词 monarkhikos，由 monarkhes「唯一统治者」加后缀 -ikos 构成，拉丁语把它改造为 -icus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos 'alone' supplies the first element of the compound, as in monologue and monopoly.
items.cn: monos「单独」提供复合词的第一个成分，与 monologue、monopoly 相同。

items.en: Arkhein 'to rule' supplies the second element, shared with hierarchy though the prefixes differ.
items.cn: arkhein「统治」提供第二个成分，与 hierarchy 共享，但前缀不同。

items.en: The adjective monarkhikos meant 'of a sole ruler' or 'fit for a ruler'.
items.cn: 形容词 monarkhikos 意为「唯一统治者的」或「适合统治者的」。

items.en: Latin reshaped Greek -ikos as -icus, the standard relational suffix that English later reduced to -ic.
items.cn: 拉丁把希腊 -ikos 改造为 -icus，这是标准的关系后缀，英语后来简化为 -ic。

items.en: English adopted the adjective beside monarchy and monarch, and later extended it to organisations and personal manner.
items.cn: 英语在 monarchy 与 monarch 旁采纳了这个形容词，后来又扩展到组织与个人作风。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation is not recorded precisely, and the organisational sense has no single documented origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证并不确切，组织义也没有唯一可考来源。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same compound or a shared element; group two holds adjectives describing rule by one person.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该复合词或共享成分的形式；第二组是描述一人统治的形容词。

entries.definition: The -ical variant of the same adjective, now the more usual form in political prose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的 -ical 变体，如今在政治文章中更常用。

entries.definition: The ruler; monarchic is the adjective derived from this person.
entries.definitionCN: 统治者；monarchic 是由这个人称派生的形容词。

entries.definition: The system or state of rule by one; the adjective can modify either this system or its ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 一人统治的制度或国家；该形容词既可修饰制度也可修饰君主。

entries.definition: From monazein 'live alone', with no arkhein element: a monastic house, not a political form.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 monazein「独居」，无 arkhein 成分：是僧院，不是政治形式。

entries.definition: Belonging to a king or queen; it names the rank, while monarchic names the constitutional type.
entries.definitionCN: 属于国王或女王；指等级，而 monarchic 指宪制类型。

entries.definition: Ruling without constitutional checks; it stresses unlimited power rather than inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 不受宪法制约地统治；强调无限权力而非世袭。

entries.definition: Ruling with arbitrary cruelty; a strongly negative word that monarchic does not always carry.
entries.definitionCN: 专横残暴地统治；贬义很强，而 monarchic 未必带有这层。

entries.definition: Arranged in ranks; it shares the arkhein element but describes any ladder, not one crown.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排列；共享 arkhein 成分，但描述任何阶梯，而非一顶王冠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monarch + -ic: the adjective of one-person rule.
normal.cn: monarch + -ic：一人统治的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs monarchic, monarchical, monarchically, monarch, monarchy, monarchist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monarchic、monarchical、monarchically、monarch、monarchy、monarchist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: monarchic system, monarchic party, monarchic structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：君主制体系、拥护君主制的政党、单一首脑结构。

normal.en: hierarchy shares arkhein but adds hieros 'sacred', so it is a cousin, not a twin.
normal.cn: hierarchy 共享 arkhein，却加了 hieros「神圣」，因此是表亲而非孪生。

normal.en: The adjective easily slips from describing a state to criticising a boss.
normal.cn: 这个形容词很容易从描述国家滑向批评上司。

abstract.en: Picture an org chart with a crown at the top and no second box.
abstract.cn: 想象一张架构图，顶端是王冠，下面没有第二个框。

abstract.en: Picture a committee where only one pen can sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会，只有一支笔能签字。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where everyone waits for one person to nod.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，所有人都等一个人点头。

examples.en: The monarchic regime lasted until the constitution was rewritten.
examples.cn: 这个君主制政权一直延续到宪法被重写。

examples.en: His monarchic gestures made the committee feel like a court.
examples.cn: 他君主般的姿态让委员会像一座宫廷。

examples.en: The report criticised the monarchic concentration of power in one office.
examples.cn: 报告批评权力君主式地集中在一个办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monarch」君主 + 「ic」的——君主式的、君主制的

root: 希腊 monarkhikos「君主的」= monarkhes「唯一统治者」+ -ikos（形容词后缀，拉丁作 -icus）；monarkhes 出自 monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」。英语 monarchic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to a person, a system, a political stance, a manner, an org chart, a state, a domineering habit and a historical era.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用到人、制度、政治立场、作风、组织图、国家、专断习性与一个历史时代上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an org chart whose top box is a crown and whose every arrow converges on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张架构图，顶端方框是王冠，所有箭头都汇向它。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the ruler and the ruler-like manner share one adjective.
branches.cn: 人：统治者与类似统治者的作风共享一个形容词。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a form of government, a state that uses it and the era it marks.
branches.cn: 制度：政府形式、采用它的国家，以及它所标记的时代。

branches.en: THE STANCE: to be monarchic is to take the crown's side in a debate.
branches.cn: 立场：持 monarchic 立场就是在辩论中站在王冠一边。

branches.en: THE ORG CHART: one signature outweighs a whole committee.
branches.cn: 组织图：一个签名重于整个委员会。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a small tyrant can reign inside an office.
branches.cn: 习性：小暴君也能在办公室里临朝。

intro.en: Monarchic is a Greek compound plus the adjective suffix -ikos, and all three parts recur in English, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: monarchic 是希腊复合词加形容词后缀 -ikos，三部分都在英语中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek monos and arkhein give monarch and monarchy; -ikos, Latin -icus, gives monarchic and hierarchical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 monos 与 arkhein 衍生 monarch 与 monarchy；-ikos（拉丁 -icus）衍生 monarchic 与 hierarchical。

items.example: The element also appears in monologue.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 中。

items.example: The root links rule to taking the lead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把统治与领头联系起来。

items.example: A monarkhes held the throne by birth.
items.exampleCN: 唯一统治者凭出生取得王位。

items.example: The suffix turns a ruler into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把统治者转为形容词。

items.example: The monarchic title passed to the son.
items.exampleCN: 君主称号传给了儿子。

items.example: The monarchical system endured.
items.exampleCN: 君主制体系延续下来。

items.example: He ruled monarchically over the department.
items.exampleCN: 他像君主一样统治这个部门。

items.example: The monarchy fell after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后君主制倾覆。

items.example: The monarch spoke briefly.
items.exampleCN: 君主简短地讲了话。

items.meaning: rule by priests, later ranked order
items.meaningCN: 祭司统治，后指等级秩序
items.example: The hierarchy was rigid.
items.exampleCN: 等级秩序很僵化。

latinEntries.structure: monarchicus, monarchica, monarchicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 按固定程序进行的一套仪式；也指仪式性的
definition_en: a set of actions performed in a fixed order, especially for religious or solemn purposes, and the adjective describing such actions
core_image: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，最年长的人先点上一炷香，其余人依次跟上
scene: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，家里最年长的人先点上一炷香。 The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
sceneCN: 这里 ritual 指「按固定程序进行的一套仪式」（第 1 个义项：有既定顺序的庄严动作）；句意为节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。可辨识物件：神龛、米碗、清水、香、钟。

pos.zh: 仪式；礼制；固定程序
仪式的；仪式性的

senses.title: A set of actions in fixed order
senses.titleCN: 按固定顺序进行的一套动作
senses.definition: a sequence of actions repeated in the same order on the same kind of occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在同类场合按同样顺序重复的一连串动作
senses.example: The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
senses.exampleCN: 节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。
senses.why: ritus named a religious rite, and the noun keeps the idea of an order that must not be varied.
senses.whyCN: ritus 指宗教仪式，这个名词保留了「顺序不可更改」的意思。

senses.title: The ordered rites of worship
senses.definition: the prescribed words and gestures of a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 宗教礼拜中规定的言辞与动作
senses.example: The priest followed the ritual exactly, down to the last bow.
senses.exampleCN: 司仪严格遵循仪式，连最后一次鞠躬也不差。
senses.why: religion is where fixed order is felt to be most necessary, so the word grew strong there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教最能感到固定顺序的必要，这个词也在此处扎根最深。

senses.title: A personal daily routine
senses.definition: a small repeated sequence that marks a part of the day, such as coffee before work
senses.definitionCN: 标记一天中某段时间的重复小序列，如上班前的咖啡
senses.example: Her morning ritual is a cup of tea and ten minutes of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的晨间固定程序是一杯茶和十分钟的安静。
senses.why: the word moved from the altar to the kitchen because both need a dependable order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从祭坛移到厨房，因为两者都需要可靠的顺序。

senses.title: Stylized social courtesy
senses.titleCN: 社会交往中的程式化礼节
senses.definition: the expected words and gestures of greeting, toasting or taking leave
senses.definitionCN: 问候、敬酒或告别时所期待的言辞与动作
senses.example: Their greeting was a ritual of three bows and two questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的问候是一套三鞠躬加两个问题的礼节。
senses.why: social life repeats its own small liturgies, and the same noun covers them.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活重复着自己的小礼序，同一个名词也就涵盖了它们。

senses.title: Rites marking a change of status
senses.titleCN: 标记身份转变的过渡仪式
senses.definition: ceremonies such as birth rites, initiation or funerals that move a person from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 出生礼、成年礼或葬礼等把人从一种状态转入另一种状态的仪式
senses.example: The initiation ritual lasted three days and ended with a new name.
senses.exampleCN: 成年仪式持续三天，最后以一个新名字结束。
senses.why: anthropology found that the most important rituals mark a crossing, not a repetition.
senses.whyCN: 人类学发现最重要的仪式标记的是跨越，而非重复。

senses.title: Repetition that has become compulsive
senses.titleCN: 仪式化的重复行为（心理层面）
senses.definition: a repeated act that calms anxiety or must be performed to avoid distress
senses.definitionCN: 为安抚焦虑而重复、或必须执行以避免痛苦的动作
senses.example: He developed a private ritual of checking the lock four times.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了一个私下的仪式：把锁检查四次。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion has the same outward shape as rite.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上相同。

senses.title: Symbolic acts that bind a group
senses.definition: public gestures such as flag-raising or oath-taking that make a group feel itself
senses.definitionCN: 升旗或宣誓等让群体感到自身存在的公开动作
senses.example: The school's Monday ritual assembled every class on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 学校周一的仪式把每个班都召集到操场上。
senses.why: a group needs a body, and repeated gestures give it one.
senses.whyCN: 群体需要一个形体，而重复的动作提供了这个形体。

senses.title: Ritual as an adjective
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of, or used in, a rite'
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示「仪式的」或「仪式中使用的」
senses.example: The ritual dance is performed only by the elders.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仪式之舞只由长者表演。
senses.why: the adjective is simply the noun doing modifying work, a common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是名词在起修饰作用，这是英语常见的转用。

senses.title: A fixed routine that feels obligatory
senses.titleCN: 例行公事般的固定做法
senses.definition: a practice repeated so often that it has lost its original purpose
senses.definitionCN: 重复得太频繁、已失去原初目的的做法
senses.example: The weekly meeting had become a ritual nobody questioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会已成了一套无人质疑的例行程序。
senses.why: when order outlives meaning, the word turns slightly ironic.
senses.whyCN: 当顺序比意义活得更久，这个词就带上了一点讽刺。

intro.en: Ritual comes from Latin ritualis 'relating to rites', from ritus 'a rite, a religious ceremony', through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritual 经古法语来自拉丁 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，而 ritualis 出自 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony, a custom'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼、惯例」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与吠陀语中表示「固定秩序」的词相联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis made a relational adjective, so ritualis meant 'belonging to a rite' and covered both books and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 ritualis 意为「属于仪式的」，书籍与动作都可用它形容。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective and noun into English, where ritual first named a book of church rites.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词与名词带入英语，ritual 最初指记载教会礼仪的书。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun meant the rites themselves, and by the nineteenth it had spread to social and personal practice.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，名词已指礼仪本身；到十九世纪，又扩展到社会与个人实践。

items.en: Both disciplines adopted the word, one for rites of passage and the other for compulsive repetition.
items.cn: 人类学与心理学都采用了这个词，前者指过渡仪式，后者指强迫性重复。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of ritus is unsettled, and the earliest use of the ironic 'mere routine' sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ritus 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，讽刺性的「只是例行公事」义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stem; group two holds terms for related solemn or repeated practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关庄严或重复做法的词。

entries.definition: One prescribed ceremony, usually religious or solemn; ritual can name the whole ordered system or the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼，通常宗教或庄严；ritual 可指整套有序体系或风格。

entries.definition: Describes something done in the manner of a rite, often with a hint of excess.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以仪式方式完成的事物，常带过度拘泥的暗示。

entries.definition: Excessive attachment to rites, or the study of them as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式的过度依附，或把仪式当作体系来研究。

entries.definition: To turn an action into a rite or to perform it in a fixed ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个动作变成仪式，或以固定礼仪方式完成。

entries.definition: A formal event with a set order; it stresses occasion and dignity more than repeated practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指有固定顺序的正式活动；比「反复实践」更强调场合与庄重。

entries.definition: The prescribed form of public religious worship, usually written down for a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 指公共宗教礼拜的规定形式，通常为会众写成文本。

entries.definition: The act of keeping a law, feast or custom; it names compliance rather than the sequence of acts.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵守法律、节期或习俗；它指遵从，而非动作序列。

entries.definition: An ordinary repeated way of doing things, without the solemn charge that ritual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指平常重复的做事方式，不带 ritual 那种庄严意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritus 'rite' plus -alis 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to a rite'.
normal.cn: ritus「仪式」加 -alis「属于……的」，得到「属于仪式的」。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: religious ritual, daily ritual, morning ritual, ritual dance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：宗教仪式、每日固定程序、晨间固定程序、仪式之舞。

normal.en: Anthropology links ritual to rites of passage: a crossing is marked, not merely repeated.
normal.cn: 人类学把仪式与过渡礼仪相连：被标记的是跨越，而不只是重复。

normal.en: The ironic sense appears when a routine outlives its reason, as in a meeting that is a ritual.
normal.cn: 当惯例活得比理由更久，讽刺义就出现，如「一场纯属仪式的会议」。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step must be taken in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级都必须按同样顺序踏过。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that rings not to tell time but to make time feel real.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，它响不是为了报时，而是让时间显得真实。

abstract.en: Picture a door that only opens when three hands touch it in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有三只手依次触碰才会打开。

examples.en: The harvest ritual begins with the youngest child pouring water.
examples.cn: 丰收仪式由最小的孩子倒水开始。

examples.en: Modern offices have their own rituals of greeting and leaving.
examples.cn: 现代办公室有自己的问候与告别仪式。

examples.en: The therapist asked whether the ritual reduced his anxiety.
examples.cn: 治疗师问他这套仪式是否减轻了焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ri（日）+ tual」——每天按同一顺序做的事，就成了仪式

root: 拉丁 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」→ ritualis「与仪式有关的」→ 古法语 → 英语 ritual。ritus 的更深来源不确定，与吠陀语「固定秩序」词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one order: a sequence that must be repeated exactly, performed at an altar, in a kitchen, in a greeting, at a crossing, in a compulsion, on a flagpole and finally in an empty meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个顺序展开：一套必须照样重复的动作，依次在祭坛、厨房、问候、人生关口、强迫行为、旗杆前上演，最后落到一场空洞的会议上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bowls laid out in a fixed order, each filled only when the previous one is full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按固定次序摆好的碗，前一只满了才轮到下一只。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: first a sequence, then the adjective that labels anything belonging to it.
branches.cn: 顺序本身：先是动作序列，再是标记任何属于该序列之物的形容词。

branches.en: ALTAR AND CROSSING: worship repeats the order, while initiation uses it to move a person.
branches.cn: 祭坛与关口：礼拜重复顺序，成年礼则用顺序移动一个人。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND EMPTY MEETING: the same order comforts a morning and hollows out a schedule.
branches.cn: 厨房与空会：同一顺序既安抚一个早晨，也掏空一张日程。

branches.en: COURTESY AND FLAG: small greetings and public gestures both make a group hold together.
branches.cn: 礼节与旗帜：小小问候与公开动作都能让群体维系。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the shape of a rite appears without its meaning, and the repetition becomes a cage.
branches.cn: 强迫：仪式的形状还在，意义却已消失，重复变成牢笼。

intro.en: Ritual is a Latin noun stem with a relational suffix, and that stem also builds the shorter noun rite and the whole ritualistic family.
intro.cn: ritual 是一个拉丁名词词干加关系后缀，同一词干还构成较短的名词 rite 与整个 ritualistic 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus supplied the stem and -alis supplied the adjective ending; English later added -istic, -ism and -ize to build manner, system and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 提供词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾；英语后来加上 -istic、-ism 与 -ize，构成方式、体系与动词。

items.example: Ritus named the ceremony before it named the style.
items.exampleCN: ritus 先指典礼，后指风格。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Ritualis covered both the book and the gestures.
items.exampleCN: ritualis 同时涵盖书与动作。

items.example: The noun grew out of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词由形容词发展而来。

items.example: Rite is the single act; ritual is the order around it.
items.exampleCN: rite 是单个行为；ritual 是围绕它的顺序。

items.example: Ritualistic means done in the manner of a rite.
items.exampleCN: ritualistic 意为以仪式的方式完成。

items.meaning: in the manner of a rite
items.example: The adjective often hints at excess.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词常暗示过度。

items.example: Ritualism names attachment to rites.
items.exampleCN: ritualism 指对仪式的依附。

items.example: Ritualize turns an act into a rite.
items.exampleCN: ritualize 把行为变成仪式。

items.example: The room was ritually cleansed before use.
items.exampleCN: 房间在使用前按仪式洁净过。

definition_zh: v. （烹饪）把油脂或肉汁浇淋在烤肉上；（缝纫）用长针脚粗缝、假缝；（旧用）痛打
definition_en: to moisten roasting meat with fat or its own juices; to join cloth with long loose temporary stitches; in older use, to thrash
core_image: 烤箱门一开，一勺滚热的盘底汁水浇回焦黄的肉面
scene: 烤箱门一开，她就把盘底的汁水浇回肉上。 She opened the oven and used the pan juices to baste the meat.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：baste 指烹饪中把油脂或汁液浇淋在烤肉上；句意是她用盘底肉汁浇淋烤肉。

pos.zh: 浇淋油脂；粗缝；痛打

senses.title: To moisten roasting meat
senses.definition: to pour fat or pan juices over meat while it cooks so that it stays moist
senses.definitionCN: 肉在烤制过程中把油脂或盘底汁液浇在其上，使其不干
senses.example: Baste the joint twice while it rests in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 肉块在炉中静置时浇两次汁。
senses.why: The kitchen sense is the newest of the three, and it is the one most readers meet first.
senses.whyCN: 厨房义是三个义项中最新的一个，也是多数读者最先遇到的。

senses.title: To sew loosely
senses.definition: to join pieces of cloth with long temporary stitches that will be removed later
senses.definitionCN: 用日后会拆掉的长针脚把布料临时缝合
senses.example: She basted the lining before machining the seam.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把衬里粗缝固定，再上机缝接缝。
senses.why: This sense comes from Old French bastir, to build or to sew loosely, so the idea is holding a shape in place.
senses.whyCN: 此义源自古法语 bastir「搭建、松缝」，核心是先把形状固定住。

senses.title: To thrash
senses.definition: in older writing, to beat someone hard
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文献中指狠打某人
senses.example: The old play has a servant basted for his insolence.
senses.exampleCN: 那出旧戏里有个仆人因无礼而被痛打。
senses.why: This verb is probably from Old Norse beysta, to beat, and it survives mainly in older texts.
senses.whyCN: 该动词可能源自古诺斯语 beysta「击打」，如今主要见于旧文献。

intro.en: Baste is really three verbs sharing one spelling: a sewing word from French, a beating word from Norse, and a kitchen word of uncertain origin that won out.
intro.cn: baste 其实是共用一个拼写的三个动词：来自法语的缝纫词、来自诺斯语的击打词，以及来源不明却最终胜出的厨房词。

items.en: Old Norse beysta meant to beat or thump, one possible source of the word.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 beysta 意为击打，是该词的一个可能来源。

items.en: Old French bastir meant to build or to sew loosely, giving the tailoring sense.
items.cn: 古法语 bastir 意为搭建或松缝，给出缝纫那一义。

items.en: Middle English uses the word for long temporary stitches holding cloth in place.
items.cn: 中古英语用该词指把布料临时固定的长针脚。

items.en: A verb meaning to thrash appears in writing, close in sound to the sewing word.
items.cn: 书面语中出现「痛打」义的动词，与缝纫词读音相近。

items.en: Cookery books use the word for moistening roasting meat with fat and juices.
items.cn: 烹饪书用该词指以油脂与肉汁浇淋烤肉。

items.en: The kitchen sense becomes the commonest, and a baster is sold as a tool for it.
items.cn: 厨房义成为最常用义，并出现名为 baster 的专用工具。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the same long vowel and the -aste shape; the near-meaning group splits into kitchen verbs and the tailoring verb, matching the two live senses.
note.cn: 形近组保留同一个长元音与 -aste 字形；近义组分为厨房动词与缝纫动词两支，正对应两个活跃义项。

entries.definition: The bottom or foundation of something.
entries.definitionCN: 底部；基础。

entries.definition: Fibre from the inner bark of trees.
entries.definitionCN: 取自树内皮的纤维。

entries.definition: A thick soft wet mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 稠厚的软糊状物。

entries.definition: Hurried speed of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙；急速。

entries.definition: To make something a little wet.
entries.definitionCN: 使略湿。

entries.definition: To sew with long loose stitches.
entries.definitionCN: 用长而松的针脚缝。

entries.definition: To coat food to give it a shine.
entries.definitionCN: 给食物涂上一层使其发亮。

entries.definition: To soak food in seasoned liquid before cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 烹调前把食物浸在调味液中。

normalIntro.en: One spelling, three jobs: wet the roast, hold the cloth, or beat the servant. Picture the spoon, the needle and the stick.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拼写，三份工作：浇湿烤肉、固定布料、痛打仆人。分别想象那把勺、那根针和那根棍。

normal.en: A spoon lifting hot juice back onto the meat.
normal.cn: 一把勺把滚热的肉汁浇回肉上。

normal.en: A needle taking long stitches that will come out.
normal.cn: 一根针缝出日后要拆掉的长针脚。

normal.en: Basted is the form you meet in recipes.
normal.cn: basted 是食谱里常见的形式。

normal.en: A baster is the little suction tool for the job.
normal.cn: baster 就是干这活的小吸油管。

normal.en: Baste rhymes with paste, and both are soft and wet.
normal.cn: baste 与 paste 押韵，两者都软而湿。

abstract.en: Care applied in small repeated doses.
abstract.cn: 以小而反复的剂量施加的照料。

abstract.en: A temporary hold that trusts a later seam.
abstract.cn: 一种信赖日后正式缝合的临时固定。

abstract.en: Keeping something from drying out while it changes.
abstract.cn: 在某物变化的过程中不让它干掉。

examples.en: Baste the chicken every half hour.
examples.cn: 每半小时给鸡浇一次汁。

examples.en: The tailor basted the sleeves in by hand.
examples.cn: 裁缝用手针把袖子粗缝上去。

examples.en: A basted roast keeps its colour better.
examples.cn: 浇过汁的烤肉色泽保持得更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝斯特」——记一把勺：烤肉时把汁浇回去就是 baste。再记一根针：缝纫的「粗缝」也叫 baste。三义一线：浇汁、假缝、（旧）痛打。

root: 一个拼写三条来源：缝纫义来自古法语 bastir「搭建、松缝」；痛打义可能来自古诺斯语 beysta「击打」；烹饪义 17 世纪见于烹饪书，来源未定，后成为最常用义并催生工具名 baster。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses that happen to share a spelling. Learn them as spoon, needle and stick, in that order of usefulness.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项恰好共用一个拼写。按「勺、针、棍」来记，顺序也正是实用程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoon of hot pan juice poured back over a browning joint
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺滚热盘汁浇回正在上色的肉块

branches.en: An oven door opened on a rush of steam.
branches.cn: 烤箱门开，热气涌出。

branches.en: A brush drawn across crisp skin.
branches.cn: 刷子在脆皮上抹过。

branches.en: Long white stitches down a lining.
branches.cn: 衬里上一行长长的白针脚。

branches.en: A servant in an old comedy.
branches.cn: 旧喜剧里的一个仆人。

branches.en: Holding moisture or shape until the end.
branches.cn: 把水分或形状保持到最后。

intro.en: Baste is a bare verb root; the endings below build its forms, its tool noun and the wider vocabulary of moistening.
intro.cn: baste 是一个赤裸的动词词根；下面这些词缀构成它的各种形式、工具名词，以及「润湿」这一语义场的更大词汇。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin bastire lies behind the French sewing verb; mare, sea, gives the brine idea in marinate, and humectare means to moisten.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bastire 是法语缝纫动词的来源；mare「海」给出 marinate 中的「盐水」构想；humectare 意为润湿。

definition_zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的；僵化的；固化的
definition_en: preserved in the form of a fossil, or, figuratively, fixed so long in one form that it can no longer change
core_image: 一片叶子落进湖底，矿物一点点填满它的细胞，千万年后只剩石头上的一道叶脉
scene: 博物馆库房的抽屉里，一片叶子的轮廓被压进灰色石板，叶脉清晰，却已没有一丝有机物残留。 The fossilized leaf in the drawer keeps every vein although nothing organic survives.
sceneCN: 这里 fossilized 指「有机体被矿物质替换、以化石形态保存下来」（第 1 个义项：生物遗体或遗迹经矿化作用定形）；句意为抽屉里的这片叶子虽保留了全部叶脉，有机物却已完全被矿物取代。可辨识物件：石板、叶脉纹、抽屉、标本签、软毛刷。

pos.zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的
僵化的；固化的；停滞不前的（比喻）
（fossilize 的过去式与过去分词）使化石化；使僵化

senses.title: Turned to stone by mineral replacement
senses.titleCN: 矿化成石：有机质被矿物替换
senses.definition: preserved as a fossil because minerals have slowly replaced the original organic material
senses.definitionCN: 因矿物缓慢替换原有有机质而以化石形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized wood still shows the grain of the original trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石化木仍能看出原树干的纹理。
senses.why: Fossil comes from Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig; the -ized ending says the thing has undergone that change and is now stone-like.
senses.whyCN: fossil 出自拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」；-ized 结尾表示该物已经历这一变化，如今状如石头。

senses.title: Preserved as a trace fossil
senses.definition: kept as a footprint, burrow, egg or other trace rather than as the body itself
senses.definitionCN: 以脚印、洞穴、蛋等遗迹而非遗体本身的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized footprints record a walk across wet ash.
senses.exampleCN: 这些化石脚印记录了一次走过湿灰地的行走。
senses.why: A trace is also fossilized when the sediment hardens around the impression; the body is gone but the shape it made has become stone.
senses.whyCN: 当沉积物在印痕周围硬化时，遗迹同样被化石化；身体不在了，它留下的形状却成了石头。

senses.title: Fixed in an outdated form
senses.titleCN: 僵化：制度或观念不再变化
senses.definition: of an institution, idea or practice, fixed so long in one shape that reform becomes impossible
senses.definitionCN: 指制度、观念或做法长期固定于一种形态，以致无法改革
senses.example: The committee had fossilized into a ritual of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会已经僵化成一道审批仪式。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the geological process: what should have decayed instead hardened, and hardening removes the ability to adapt.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了地质过程：本该腐朽的东西反而硬化了，而硬化剥夺了适应能力。

senses.title: Stuck in old habits
senses.titleCN: 停滞：人停留在旧习惯里
senses.definition: of a person or group, no longer able to change because habits have hardened
senses.definitionCN: 指人或群体因习惯硬化而不再能改变
senses.example: He had fossilized in his opinions by the age of forty.
senses.exampleCN: 他四十岁时观念就已僵化。
senses.why: The same image applied to a mind: repeated behaviour sets like cement, and the set shape resists new evidence.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象用于心智：重复的行为像水泥一样凝固，凝固的形状抗拒新证据。

senses.title: A form frozen in a language
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, kept in an earlier form inside a fixed expression
senses.definitionCN: 指词或短语在固定表达中以较早的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized phrase still uses a verb form no one speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个固化短语仍使用无人再说的动词形式。
senses.why: Languages preserve dead forms inside idioms the way rock preserves shells: the surrounding expression stops the change.
senses.whyCN: 语言在习语中保存已死的形式，就像岩石保存贝壳：周围的表达阻止了变化。

senses.title: Dated and unable to update
senses.titleCN: 定型的：因年代久远而无法更新
senses.definition: of a system or style, preserved in an earlier state and unable to modernise
senses.definitionCN: 指体系或风格停留在较早状态、无法现代化
senses.example: The fossilized software could not read any file made after two thousand five.
senses.exampleCN: 这套固化的软件读不了那一年之后生成的任何文件。
senses.why: Systems also harden: once dependencies set, every later change costs more than the system can pay, so the old shape survives.
senses.whyCN: 系统也会硬化：依赖一旦固定，此后每次改动的代价都超出系统所能支付，旧形状便存活下来。

senses.title: Bone filled with mineral
senses.definition: of bone, shell or tooth, with its pores filled by mineral so that the original shape is kept
senses.definitionCN: 指骨骼、贝壳或牙齿的孔隙被矿物充填，从而保留原形
senses.example: The fossilized tooth is heavy because mineral fills every pore.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗化石牙很重，因为矿物填满了每个孔隙。
senses.why: Hard parts fossilize best because they already contain mineral; groundwater adds more, and the object gains weight and permanence.
senses.whyCN: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为它们本就含矿物；地下水再添矿物，物件便增加重量与持久性。

senses.title: Frozen in a single moment
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything that seems arrested at one moment and never moves on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻任何仿佛停在一刻、再也不向前的事物
senses.example: The village felt fossilized in the decade the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 这座村庄仿佛冻结在矿场关闭的那个年代。
senses.why: The image reaches its limit here: not merely old, but arrested, as if time had stopped and left the object inside a single layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象在此达到极限：不只是旧，而是被定格，仿佛时间停止，把物件封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is the past participle of fossilize, built on fossil plus the suffix -ize. Fossil goes back to Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fossilized 是 fossilize 的过去分词，由 fossil 加后缀 -ize 构成。fossil 上溯拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fodere meant to dig; its participle fossus, dug, produced fossilis, a thing dug out of the earth.
items.cn: fodere 意为挖掘；其分词 fossus「被挖的」产生 fossilis，即从地里挖出之物。

items.en: Fossilis named anything obtained by digging, including stones and buried remains; English adopted it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: fossilis 指任何挖掘所得之物，包括石头与埋藏的遗存；英语在十七世纪引入这个词。

items.en: As geology took shape, fossil narrowed to the preserved traces of organisms, and fossilize was coined for the process that produces them.
items.cn: 随着地质学成形，fossil 收窄为生物遗存的保存形态，fossilize 则为产生这一形态的过程而造。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the participle was already used of institutions and opinions that had hardened beyond change.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这一分词已用于形容硬化到无法改变的制度与观念。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single author is credited with coining fossilize, and the date of its first geological use is not fixed; the suffix -ize was freely added to nouns in that period.
items.cn: 来源不确定：没有辞书把 fossilize 的创造归给某一位作者，其首次地质学用法也无定年；当时 -ize 后缀可自由加在名词上。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same fossil stock; the second group holds words for things that have stopped changing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fossil 词干的词；第二组是表示「不再变化」的词。

entries.definition: The preserved remains itself; fossilized describes the state the remains reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指保存下来的遗存本身；fossilized 描述它达到的状态。

entries.definition: The process verb, to turn into a fossil or to become rigid; the participle names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 过程动词，指变成化石或变得僵硬；分词形式指结果。

entries.definition: From the same fodere, to dig, but it describes animals adapted for digging, not preserved remains.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 fodere「挖掘」，但形容适应掘土的动物，而非保存下来的遗存。

entries.definition: Literally turned to stone by mineral replacement; it is the closest physical synonym, while fossilized can also mean trace-preserved.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指被矿物替换成石头；它是最接近的物理同义词，而 fossilized 也可指遗迹保存。

entries.definition: Stiff and unwilling to bend; it describes the behaviour, while fossilized adds the image of geological hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬、不愿弯曲；它描述行为，而 fossilized 增加了地质硬化的意象。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned and out of use; it says nothing about hardening, only about surviving past its time.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧而不再使用；它不涉及硬化，只说明活过了它的时代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the digging root, the -ize suffix, the trace fossils, and the metaphor of hardening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示挖掘的词根、-ize 后缀、遗迹化石，以及硬化的比喻。

normal.en: fodere, to dig, gives fossilis, dug up: a fossil is literally something dug out of the ground.
normal.cn: fodere「挖掘」派生 fossilis「被挖出的」：化石字面就是从地里挖出的东西。

normal.en: -ize turns the noun into a process, and -ed marks the result: the thing has been through the process.
normal.cn: -ize 把名词变成过程，-ed 标记结果：该物已经历这一过程。

normal.en: Body fossils keep the organism; trace fossils keep what it did, such as footprints and burrows.
normal.cn: 实体化石保存生物本身；遗迹化石保存它做过的事，如脚印与洞穴。

normal.en: Hard parts fossilize best because bone and shell already contain mineral.
normal.cn: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为骨与壳本就含矿物。

normal.en: Applied to people, the same word accuses them of having hardened instead of growing.
normal.cn: 用于人时，同一个词是在指责他们硬化了，而不是成长了。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fossilization is change that stops: the object keeps its shape by losing its capacity to respond.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，化石化是停止的变化：物件靠失去回应能力来保住形状。

abstract.en: Preservation and death are the same process seen from two sides: what survives is what could not decay.
abstract.cn: 保存与死亡是同一过程的两面：活下来的，正是无法腐朽的部分。

abstract.en: Every institution should ask whether its stability is growth or fossilization.
abstract.cn: 每个机构都该问：它的稳定是成长，还是僵化。

examples.en: The fossilized reef shows that a warm sea once covered this desert.
examples.cn: 这片石化礁石说明温暖的海曾覆盖过这片沙漠。

examples.en: Fossilized pollen in the sediment records the plants of that era.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的化石花粉记录了那个时代的植物。

examples.en: The department had fossilized around a procedure no one could defend.
examples.cn: 这个部门围绕一道无人能辩护的程序僵化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fossil（化石）+ ized（已经变成）」——已经变成化石的 → 化石化的、僵化的

root: 拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」（源于 fodere「挖掘」）+ 动词后缀 -ize 的过去分词 -ized；字面为「已被挖出、已成化石的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hardening: organic matter becomes stone, a trace becomes stone, and then institutions, minds, phrases, systems and whole places become unable to change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次硬化展开：有机物变成石头，遗迹变成石头，随后制度、心智、短语、系统乃至整个地方都变得无法改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft tissue replaced grain by grain until only a stone copy remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软组织被一粒粒矿物替换，最后只剩一份石质副本。

branches.en: THE BODY IN STONE: replacement and pore-filling are two routes to the same heavy copy.
branches.cn: 石中的身体：替换与充填是通往同一份沉重副本的两条路。

branches.en: THE SHAPE LEFT BEHIND: a footprint hardens into evidence even when no body is there.
branches.cn: 留下的形状：即使没有身体，脚印也会硬化成证据。

branches.en: HARDENED INSTITUTIONS AND MINDS: what should have adapted instead set like cement.
branches.cn: 硬化的制度与心智：本该适应的东西却像水泥一样凝固。

branches.en: THE IDIOM AS AMBER: a fixed phrase preserves a dead form exactly as resin preserves an insect.
branches.cn: 习语如琥珀：固定短语保存已死的形式，正如树脂保存昆虫。

branches.en: ARRESTED TIME: systems and places stop updating and seem sealed inside one layer.
branches.cn: 被定格的时间：系统与地方停止更新，仿佛被封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is transparent: a Latin-derived noun, a productive verb suffix and a past-participle ending.
intro.cn: fossilized 的构造很透明：一个拉丁来源的名词、一个能产动词后缀与一个过去分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin fodere, to dig, gives fossilis and then fossil; English adds -ize and -ed. The same fodere also gives fossorial, describing digging animals.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fodere「挖掘」衍生 fossilis，再进入英语为 fossil；英语加上 -ize 与 -ed。同一 fodere 还衍生 fossorial，形容掘土动物。

items.example: Fodere is the source of fossil and fossorial.
items.exampleCN: fodere 是 fossil 与 fossorial 的来源。

items.example: Fossilis described stones taken from deep ground.
items.exampleCN: fossilis 形容从深土中取出的石头。

items.example: The fossil was found in marine limestone.
items.exampleCN: 这块化石发现于海相石灰岩中。

items.example: Fossil plus -ize means to become a fossil.
items.exampleCN: fossil 加 -ize 意为变成化石。

items.meaning: to turn into a fossil, or to become rigid
items.example: Wood can fossilize in mineral-rich water.
items.exampleCN: 木材在富含矿物质的水中可以化石化。

items.example: The -ed ending marks the completed process.
items.exampleCN: -ed 词尾标记已完成的过程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fossil
items.example: Fossilization needs rapid burial and mineral water.
items.exampleCN: 化石化需要迅速埋藏与含矿物质的水。

items.example: The fossiliferous layer is dark and hard.
items.exampleCN: 含化石的层位颜色深、质地硬。

items.example: Fossorial mammals have strong forelimbs.
items.exampleCN: 掘土哺乳动物前肢强壮。

items.example: The fosse around the fort is still visible.
items.exampleCN: 堡垒周围的壕沟仍可见。

definition_zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体；发掘与登记档案
definition_en: the surviving body of material remains and the documentation of excavations, taken together as the record of the human past
core_image: 一面墙的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边是一排写满层位与坐标的登记册
scene: 库房的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边一摞登记册写满层位与坐标。 The archaeological record fills the shelves with numbered boxes and matching registers.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeological record 指「留存下来的物质遗存与发掘记录合在一起构成的总体」（第 1 个义项：作为人类过去之记录的物质与文献总和）；句意为架上的编号纸盒与对应登记册共同构成这份记录。可辨识物件：纸盒、编号签、登记册、铅笔、层位表。

pos.zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体（不可数）
（某一地区或某次发掘的）记录材料

senses.title: The surviving material record
senses.titleCN: 物质遗存总体：留存下来的全部物质材料
senses.definition: everything that survives from past human activity and can be studied as a body of material
senses.definitionCN: 过去人类活动中留存下来、可作为材料总体研究的一切
senses.example: Forests and cities both leave different traces in the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 森林与城市在考古记录中留下不同的痕迹。
senses.why: Record comes from Latin recordari, to remember, built on cor, heart: the word treats matter as a memory that the earth kept.
senses.whyCN: record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」，其词根是 cor「心」：这个词把物质当作大地保存下来的记忆。

senses.title: The field documentation
senses.titleCN: 田野记录：发掘现场的表格与笔记
senses.definition: the notes, plans, sections and photographs made while a site is being dug
senses.definitionCN: 发掘过程中所做的笔记、平面图、剖面图与照片
senses.example: The archaeological record for the trench fills four notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个探方的田野记录写满了四个笔记本。
senses.why: Digging destroys the deposit, so the written record must replace what the spade removes; documentation is the site's second life.
senses.whyCN: 发掘会毁掉堆积，因此文字记录必须替代铁锹移走的东西；档案就是遗址的第二次生命。

senses.title: The published literature
senses.titleCN: 已发表记录：正式出版的研究材料
senses.definition: the published reports and articles through which a dig becomes available to other researchers
senses.definitionCN: 使一次发掘可为其他研究者使用的正式报告与论文
senses.example: Much of the archaeological record is known only through old reports.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录的很大部分只能通过旧报告得知。
senses.why: An unpublished dig is nearly invisible; publication is what turns private notes into a public record.
senses.whyCN: 未发表的发掘几乎不可见；出版才把私人笔记变成公共记录。

senses.title: The register and database
senses.titleCN: 登记册与数据库：编目化的记录
senses.definition: the catalogued list of sites, finds and contexts held in a register or database
senses.definitionCN: 以登记册或数据库形式保存的地点、发现物与情境目录
senses.example: The national archaeological record lists every known burial mound.
senses.exampleCN: 全国考古记录列出了每一处已知的墓葬土丘。
senses.why: Once entries are numbered and indexed, the record becomes searchable, and a searchable past is a different kind of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦条目被编号并建立索引，记录就变得可检索，而可检索的过去是另一种证据。

senses.title: The regional sequence
senses.titleCN: 区域序列：某地区遗存的年代序列
senses.definition: the ordered succession of material from one region, used to place finds in time
senses.definitionCN: 某地区材料的先后序列，用于把发现物定位到时间中
senses.example: The island's archaeological record runs from early farming to the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的考古记录从早期农耕延续到青铜时代。
senses.why: Materials from one area accumulate into a sequence, and that sequence becomes the local ruler against which new finds are measured.
senses.whyCN: 同一地区的材料累积成序列，这个序列就成为衡量新发现的地方标尺。

senses.title: Bias and incompleteness
senses.titleCN: 偏差与不完整：记录本身的偏向
senses.definition: the distortion in the record caused by what survives, what is found and what is published
senses.definitionCN: 因何物留存、何物被发现、何物被发表而造成的记录偏差
senses.example: Stone survives better, so the archaeological record overstates stone tools.
senses.exampleCN: 石头更易保存，因此考古记录夸大了石器的比重。
senses.why: The record is a sample, not a census: decay, discovery and publication each filter it, and every filter leaves a bias.
senses.whyCN: 记录是样本而非普查：腐朽、发现与发表各是一道筛子，每道筛子都留下偏差。

senses.title: Curation of the archive
senses.titleCN: 档案保存：记录被长期维护的状态
senses.definition: the state of being kept, conserved and made accessible in a museum or archive
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆或档案馆中被保存、修复并可查阅的状态
senses.example: Poor curation has already damaged part of the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 保存不善已经损坏了部分考古记录。
senses.why: Documentation and objects decay too, so the record needs care; curation is what keeps a past record from becoming a future loss.
senses.whyCN: 档案与物件也会衰败，因此记录需要照料；保存工作防止过去的记录变成未来的损失。

senses.title: The record as a research archive
senses.titleCN: 作为研究资料库的记录
senses.definition: the accumulated body of material and data reused for new questions long after the original dig
senses.definitionCN: 原始发掘结束很久之后，仍被用于新问题的材料与数据总体
senses.example: Old samples in the archaeological record answered a new question about diet.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录中的旧样本回答了一个关于饮食的新问题。
senses.why: Good records outlive their questions; the archive becomes a mine that later researchers can reopen with new tools.
senses.whyCN: 好的记录比它最初的问题活得更久；资料库成为后来者可用新工具重开的矿。

intro.en: Archaeological record joins Greek archaeology, the study of ancient things, with record, from Latin recordari, to remember. The phrase treats material and documents as one memory of the past. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeological record 把希腊来源的 archaeology（研究古代事物）与 record 连在一起；record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」。这个短语把物质与文献当成同一份关于过去的记忆。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cor, genitive cordis, meant heart, and the Romans placed memory in the heart; recordari meant to remember, literally to bring back to the heart.
items.cn: cor（属格 cordis）意为心，罗马人把记忆安置在心里；recordari 意为记住，字面是「重新带回心里」。

items.en: Recordari, built on re-, back, plus cor, produced recorder in Old French and record in English, first as a verb and then as a noun.
items.cn: recordari 由 re-「回」加 cor 构成，经古法语 recorder 产生英语 record，先作动词，后作名词。

items.en: Arkhaios, ancient, plus logos, account, gave the name of the discipline that studies material remains.
items.cn: arkhaios「古老」加 logos「叙述」，构成研究物质遗存之学科的名称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century archaeologists began to speak of a record because the surviving material could be read like an archive, with entries, gaps and losses.
items.cn: 十九世纪考古学者开始谈「记录」，因为留存材料可以像档案一样阅读，有条目、空缺与散失。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date at which the phrase became standard is not documented, and the metaphor of material as a record has been criticised as misleading by later scholars.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语成为标准说法的年代没有文献记载，而把物质比作记录的做法后来也受到学者批评，认为会误导。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that name parts or views of the same archive; the second group holds words for bodies of stored information.
note.cn: 第一组是命名同一档案之部分或视角的短语；第二组是表示储存信息总体的词。

entries.definition: The portion of the record used to support one specific claim; the record is the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 记录中用于支持某一具体论断的部分；记录是整体。

entries.definition: The systematic search that adds new entries to the record rather than the record itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为记录增添新条目的系统搜寻，而非记录本身。

entries.definition: The documentation for a single site, a small unit inside the larger record.
entries.definitionCN: 单个遗址的档案，是更大记录中的一个小编单位。

entries.definition: An organised store of documents; the archaeological record includes objects as well as documents.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的文献储存；考古记录除文献外还包括实物。

entries.definition: A structured set of searchable entries; it is one modern form of the record, not its whole content.
entries.definitionCN: 可检索条目的结构化集合；它是记录的现代形式之一，而非全部内容。

entries.definition: Evidence given by a witness; it is human speech, while the archaeological record is mostly mute matter.
entries.definitionCN: 证人提供的证据；它出自人的言说，而考古记录多半是无声的物质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the heart-rooted memory word, the Greek discipline, the filters of decay and the archive that outlives its dig.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：以「心」为根的记忆词、希腊学科、腐朽造成的筛子，以及比发掘活得更久的档案。

normal.en: recordari, to remember, from cor, heart: the record is the earth's memory.
normal.cn: recordari「记住」出自 cor「心」：记录就是大地的记忆。

normal.en: Archaeology is the Greek account of ancient things, and the record is what that account is built on.
normal.cn: archaeology 是希腊语「关于古代事物的叙述」，记录正是这项叙述的立足处。

normal.en: Digging destroys, so the written record must stand in for what the spade removed.
normal.cn: 发掘会毁坏，因此文字记录必须代替铁锹移走的部分。

normal.en: Three filters shape it: what survives, what is found, what is published.
normal.cn: 三道筛子塑造它：什么留存下来、什么被发现、什么被发表。

normal.en: A good archive outlives its original question and can be reopened later.
normal.cn: 好的档案比它最初的问题活得更久，日后还能被重新打开。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a record is a sample pretending to be a census, and its gaps are as informative as its entries.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，记录是伪装成普查的样本，它的空缺与条目同样有信息量。

abstract.en: The word fuses matter and memory: what is kept is at once an object and a statement.
abstract.cn: 这个词把物质与记忆熔在一起：被保存的东西既是物件，也是陈述。

abstract.en: Every archive decides what the future will be able to ask.
abstract.cn: 每座档案库都在决定未来能提出什么问题。

examples.en: Coastal sites are poorly represented in the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 海岸遗址在考古记录中所占比例很低。

examples.en: The excavation was never published, so it barely enters the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 这次发掘从未发表，因此几乎未进入考古记录。

examples.en: New dating methods let researchers re-read the same archaeological record.
examples.cn: 新的测年方法让研究者重读同一份考古记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考古（archaeology）+ 记录（record）」——埋在地下、又被写进册子的全部痕迹 → 考古记录

root: 希腊 arkhaios「古老的」+ logos「叙述」构成 archaeology；拉丁 recordari「记住」（re- + cor「心」）构成 record；字面为「关于古代遗存的记忆总体」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one archive: matter survives, diggers write it down, reports publish it, registers index it, regions order it, filters bias it, curators keep it and later researchers reopen it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座档案库展开：物质留存，发掘者记下，报告发表，登记册编目，区域排序，筛子造成偏差，保管者维护，后来者重开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered boxes on a shelf beside registers that describe them.
core.cn: 核心意象：架上的编号纸盒，旁边是描述它们的登记册。

branches.en: MATTER AND ORDER: the surviving body gains meaning only when arranged into a regional sequence.
branches.cn: 物质与秩序：留存总体只有排成区域序列才获得意义。

branches.en: WRITING REPLACES DIGGING: notes and reports preserve what the spade destroyed.
branches.cn: 书写替代挖掘：笔记与报告保存了铁锹毁掉的东西。

branches.en: THE INDEX: numbering turns a heap into a searchable record.
branches.cn: 索引：编号把一堆东西变成可检索的记录。

branches.en: THE FILTERS: decay, discovery and publication bias the sample, and care is needed to keep what remains.
branches.cn: 筛子：腐朽、发现与发表使样本带偏，而留存部分需要照料。

branches.en: THE REOPENED MINE: an archive outlives its questions and serves new ones.
branches.cn: 重开的矿：档案比它的问题活得更久，并服务于新问题。

intro.en: Archaeological record is a Greek-Latin hybrid phrase: the discipline from Greek and the memory word from Latin.
intro.cn: archaeological record 是一个希腊—拉丁混合短语：学科名来自希腊语，记忆之词来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos build archaeology; Latin re- and cor build record, recordari and recorder. English record then extends to recording, recorded and recordation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 构成 archaeology；拉丁 re- 与 cor 构成 record、recordari、recorder。英语 record 再扩展出 recording、recorded、recordation。

items.example: Arkhaios marks what belongs to an early age.
items.exampleCN: arkhaios 标记属于早期时代之物。

items.example: Logos gives the -logy of archaeology.
items.exampleCN: logos 为 archaeology 提供 -logy。

items.example: Archaeology depends on careful recording.
items.exampleCN: 考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.example: Cor is the root of record and cordial.
items.exampleCN: cor 是 record 与 cordial 的词根。

items.meaning: to remember, to call back to mind
items.example: Recordari is the source of English record.
items.exampleCN: recordari 是英语 record 的来源。

items.meaning: to set down, or a written account
items.example: Every find is recorded with coordinates.
items.exampleCN: 每件发现物都连坐标一起记录。

items.meaning: the act or product of setting down
items.example: Good recording saves a site from oblivion.
items.exampleCN: 良好的记录使遗址免于湮没。

items.meaning: set down in writing or data
items.example: The wall is recorded in plan and section.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙被记录在平面图与剖面图中。

items.example: The recorder noted the depth of each layer.
items.exampleCN: 记录员记下每一层的深度。

items.example: Recordation of the find took a full day.
items.exampleCN: 这件发现物的登记记录花了一整天。

definition_zh: 证券；可交易的金融工具（股票、债券等）
definition_en: tradable financial instruments, such as shares and bonds
core_image: 一叠盖着印章的凭证，每一张都能在市场上换成钱
scene: 听证会上，监管人员指出这家公司向公众出售可交易的投资凭证时没有充分披露风险。 The regulator accused the firm of selling securities without proper disclosure.
sceneCN: 这里指「可交易的金融工具」，对应第 1 个义项：股票、债券等可在市场上买卖的凭证；句意为监管者指控该公司出售证券时未充分披露信息。画面要点：成叠凭证、监管徽章、披露文件。

pos.zh: 证券（复数形式，统指股票、债券等可交易金融工具）

derivatives.zh: 安全；保障；单数形式的证券
把资产打包成可交易证券

senses.title: Tradable financial instruments as a class
senses.titleCN: 作为一类可交易金融工具
senses.definition: financial instruments that can be bought and sold in markets, such as shares and bonds
senses.definitionCN: 可在市场上买卖的金融工具，如股票与债券
senses.example: Banks must hold enough capital against their securities.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须为其证券持有足够的资本。
senses.why: The plural of security names instruments that make an investor feel secure because they can be sold or redeemed; the abstract assurance becomes a countable paper claim.
senses.whyCN: security 的复数指那些因可出售或可兑付而让投资者安心的工具；抽象的保障于是变成可计数的纸面权利。

senses.title: Debt securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent a loan to an issuer, such as bonds and notes
senses.definitionCN: 代表向发行人提供贷款的工具，如债券与票据
senses.example: The fund shifted from shares into debt securities.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金从股票转向债务证券。
senses.why: One branch of the class is pure borrowing: the holder has lent money and holds a right to interest and repayment.
senses.whyCN: 这一类中的一支是纯粹的借贷：持有人借出了资金，握有收取利息与收回本金的权利。

senses.title: Equity securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent ownership in a company, such as shares
senses.definitionCN: 代表公司所有权的工具，如股票
senses.example: Equity securities carry voting rights and dividend claims.
senses.exampleCN: 权益证券带有表决权与股息主张。
senses.why: The other branch is ownership rather than lending: the holder owns a portion of the company and shares in its fortunes.
senses.whyCN: 另一支是所有权而非借贷：持有人拥有公司的一部分，并与其命运与共。

senses.title: Government securities
senses.definition: debt instruments issued by a government or its agencies
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或其机构发行的债务工具
senses.example: During the crisis investors rushed into government securities.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间投资者涌向政府证券。
senses.why: The class is narrowed by the issuer: the same instrument is backed by the taxing power of a state rather than by a company.
senses.whyCN: 这一类按发行人收窄：同样的工具由国家征税能力而非公司信用支撑。

senses.title: Certificates of ownership
senses.definition: documents that evidence a right to a share or an asset
senses.definitionCN: 证明对股份或资产享有权利的文件
senses.example: The old certificates were replaced by electronic securities.
senses.exampleCN: 旧式纸质凭证被电子证券取代。
senses.why: Before computers the security was a physical paper that proved the claim, which is the literal root of the financial sense.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机之前，证券就是证明权利的一纸实物，这正是金融义的字面来源。

senses.title: Legal instruments promising payment
senses.definition: legal documents such as promissory notes that bind a party to pay
senses.definitionCN: 本票等把一方约束在付款义务上的法律文书
senses.example: The merchant deposited the securities with his bank.
senses.exampleCN: 商人把那些付款凭证存进了银行。
senses.why: In commercial law a security can be a written promise to pay, so the same plural covers paper that creates a legal obligation.
senses.whyCN: 在商法中，证券也可以是一纸付款承诺，因此同一个复数形式也涵盖产生法律义务的文书。

senses.title: Assets pledged as collateral
senses.definition: assets deposited to guarantee a loan or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 为担保贷款或义务而交存的资产
senses.example: He pledged his securities against the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他用自己的证券为这笔贷款作担保。
senses.why: Here the instrument is used as a shield: the lender holds the security so that a default can be covered by selling it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的工具被当作盾牌：出借人握有担保品，违约时便可出售以弥补损失。

senses.title: The securities industry
senses.definition: the sector of firms that issue, trade or advise on such instruments
senses.definitionCN: 发行、交易或为此类工具提供咨询的行业
senses.example: She spent twenty years working in securities.
senses.exampleCN: 她在证券行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: A mass of instruments and the firms handling them come to be named by the instruments themselves, so the plural stands for an entire trade.
senses.whyCN: 大量工具与处理这些工具的机构，最终以工具本身来命名，于是复数形式代表整个行业。

intro.en: Securities is the plural of security, a word built on Latin cura 'care' with the prefix se- 'without'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: securities 是 security 的复数；security 由拉丁语 cura「忧虑、照料」加前缀 se-「无」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cura meant care, concern or anxiety, and it built words about protecting against trouble.
items.cn: cura 意为照料、忧虑、担心，构成了一批表示防患于未然的词。

items.en: Securitas meant freedom from care or anxiety, a state in which nothing threatens.
items.cn: securitas 意为无忧无虑、免于焦虑，是一种没有威胁的状态。

items.en: Through French the word entered English as a state of safety or certainty, and later as a guarantee against loss.
items.cn: 经法语进入英语后，它先指安全或确定的状态，后来指防损失的保证。

items.en: Tradable claims on debt or ownership came to be called securities because a paper certificate gave the holder assurance of value.
items.cn: 可交易的债权或所有权凭证被称为 securities，因为一纸证书给了持有人关于价值的保障。

items.en: Company and securities law separated the traded instrument from the general idea of safety, fixing the plural as a technical term.
items.cn: 公司法与证券法把可交易工具与一般「安全」概念分开，使复数形式固定为专业术语。

note.en: The first group shares the same root or looks nearly identical; the second group lists other financial instruments and nearby categories.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或拼写几乎相同；第二组列出其他金融工具与相邻类别。

entries.definition: The singular can mean safety, a guarantee, or one financial instrument; the plural usually means the instruments as a class.
entries.definitionCN: 单数可指安全、保证或一件金融工具；复数通常指作为一类的金融工具。

entries.definition: A guarantee or a person who guarantees another's obligation; it is about backing a promise, not about traded paper.
entries.definitionCN: 担保或为他人义务作保的人；它关乎为承诺作保，而非可交易凭证。

entries.definition: Safe, or to make safe; it keeps the original sense of freedom from danger and lacks the financial plural.
entries.definitionCN: 安全的，或使安全；保留「免于危险」的原义，没有金融上的复数用法。

entries.definition: The process of pooling assets and issuing tradable securities backed by them; it is the action, not the instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 把资产打包并发行以其为支撑的可交易证券的过程；它是动作，不是工具本身。

entries.definition: Shares, treated as a class; equities are one kind of security, not the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的股份；股票是证券的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: Debt instruments issued by governments or companies; bonds are another kind of security.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或公司发行的债务工具；债券是证券的另一类。

entries.definition: A general finance term for contracts and documents with monetary value; securities is the narrower legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 金融中对具有货币价值的合约与文书的统称；证券是更窄的法律类别。

entries.definition: Anything bought to produce a return, including property and gold; securities are only the tradable paper part.
entries.definitionCN: 为产生回报而购买的任何东西，包括房产与黄金；证券只是其中可交易的那部分纸面资产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root for care, real fixed phrases and real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「忧虑」词根、真实固定搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Security first meant freedom from care; a paper that removes worry about value became a security.
normal.cn: security 本义是免于忧虑；能消除价值担忧的一纸凭证便成了证券。

normal.en: The plural is the class word: stocks, bonds and notes are all securities.
normal.cn: 复数形式是类名词：股票、债券与票据都是证券。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the field: securities market, securities firm, securities law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给这个领域分类：证券市场、证券公司、证券法。

normal.en: Securities can be debt or equity, which are two ways of holding a claim.
normal.cn: 证券可以是债务或权益，这是持有权利的两种方式。

normal.en: Pledged securities act as collateral, so the word returns to its old sense of guarantee.
normal.cn: 用作质押的证券充当担保品，这个词于是回到它古老的「保证」义。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet of stamped papers, each able to turn into money at a shout.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠盖印的纸，每一张都能在一声喊价中变成钱。

abstract.en: Picture the paper dissolving into a number on a screen, still carrying the same claim.
abstract.cn: 想象纸张消融成屏幕上的一串数字，却仍携带同样的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a promise and an ownership share drawn as two different keys to the same lock.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺与所有权份额画成开同一把锁的两把不同钥匙。

examples.en: The firm was fined for misleading buyers of securities.
examples.cn: 该公司因误导证券买家而被罚款。

examples.en: Foreign investors may purchase government securities freely.
examples.cn: 外国投资者可以自由购买政府证券。

examples.en: She keeps a small part of her savings in securities.
examples.cn: 她把一小部分储蓄放在证券上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安心」的凭证——拿着它，价值有保障，还能在市场上卖掉 → 证券

root: security 出自拉丁语 securitas「无忧、安全」，由 se-「无」加 cura「忧虑、照料」构成；后指能带来价值保障的书面凭证，复数 securities 固定为证券。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide the class by what the paper represents: a tradable claim, a loan, an ownership share, a state-backed debt, a certificate, a promise to pay, a pledge and an entire industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按纸面所代表的东西来划分这一类：可交易权利、贷款、所有权份额、国家背书的债务、凭证、付款承诺、质押品与整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of stamped papers, each convertible into money at a shout.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠盖章的纸，每一张都能在喊价中换成钱。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the plural names tradable financial instruments as a whole.
branches.cn: 类别：复数形式统称可交易的金融工具。

branches.en: LENDING BRANCH: debt securities, including those issued by governments, represent money lent.
branches.cn: 借贷分支：债务证券，包括政府发行的债务证券，代表借出的资金。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP BRANCH: equity securities and share certificates represent a portion owned.
branches.cn: 所有权分支：权益证券与股份凭证代表所拥有的一部分。

branches.en: LEGAL PAPER: a promise to pay or an asset pledged as collateral turns the instrument into a safeguard.
branches.cn: 法律纸面：付款承诺或作为质押品的资产，把工具变成一种保障。

branches.en: TRADE AS A WHOLE: the instruments give their name to the industry that deals in them.
branches.cn: 整体行业：这些工具把名字给了经营它们的行业。

intro.en: Securities belongs to the Latin family of cura, and its derived words move between safety, guarantee and the packaging of assets.
intro.cn: securities 属于拉丁语 cura 一族，其派生词在安全、担保与资产打包之间移动。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura gives security, surety, assure and secure; the prefix se- adds the sense of being free from care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 衍生出 security、surety、assure 与 secure；前缀 se- 增添「免于忧虑」的意思。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of freedom from worry.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着免于忧虑的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns safe into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「安全」变成一种状态。

items.example: They secured the door before leaving.
items.exampleCN: 他们离开前把门锁好。

items.example: The guard provides security at night.
items.exampleCN: 警卫在夜间提供安保。

items.example: The bank trades securities.
