senses.title: An idea occurring after the event
senses.titleCN: 事后想起的想法；事后补充
senses.definition: a remark or item added when the main part is already done, showing it was not planned in advance
senses.definitionCN: 主要部分完成之后才补上的一句话或一项内容，说明事先并未计划
senses.example: She asked about the venue first and mentioned the dress code as an afterthought.
senses.exampleCN: 她先问了地点，末了才顺口补了句着装要求。
senses.why: The compound is literal: a thought that arrives after. Its core image is the missed item remembered too late.
senses.whyCN: 复合词结构即字面义：「之后」才到来的「想法」；核心画面是事过之后才想起的遗漏。

senses.title: Something given too little and too late
senses.titleCN: 不被重视的次要事物；临时敷衍的添加
senses.definition: something added carelessly at the end and treated as unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 末尾随手加上、被当作无关紧要的东西
senses.example: Accessibility was an afterthought in the design, bolted on at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 无障碍设计在这套方案里只是事后补丁，最后一刻才草草加上。
senses.why: Because an afterthought was never planned, it is by definition second-class; the word turned that defect into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 既然是「事后才想起」，就注定不是重点；词义由此转出批评色彩——「敷衍的、次要的添加」。

intro.en: A transparent English compound of after plus thought, modelled on earlier after-words.
intro.cn: 一目了然的英语复合词：after（之后）+ thought（想法），仿照更早的 after- 系词构成。

items.en: The root *terk- (to twist, to form) is generally linked to think and thought.
items.cn: 一般认为 think / thought 与重构词根 *terk-（搓转、成形）相关。

items.en: after and þoht existed separately; compounds with after- named whatever followed.
items.cn: 古英语中 after 与 þoht 各自独立；after- 系复合词命名「随后出现的事物」。

items.en: afterthought appears in the sense of later reflection, sometimes regret.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 afterthought，意为「事后的思索」，有时带悔意。

items.en: The sense settled on an addition made afterwards, often contrasted with forethought.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪词义固定为「事后添加」，常与 forethought（预先考虑）相对。

items.en: The phrase as an afterthought is idiomatic; the word often criticises neglected priorities.
items.cn: 现代英语中 as an afterthought 已成语化；该词常用于批评被忽视的优先事项。

note.en: Afterthought is the mirror of forethought; it differs from a simple addition by arriving late and unplanned.
note.cn: afterthought 与 forethought 互为镜像；它与普通的「补充」不同，在于来得晚且不在计划内。

definition_zh: 偿还；还款；报答；回报
definition_en: to pay back money owed; to give something in return for kindness or injury
core_image: 一只张开的手掌接到钱，另一张手掌上的欠款数字随之变小
scene: 小方大学时向亲戚借了一笔钱，毕业工作的第一个月就想把它还掉。 He plans to repay the entire debt within two years.
sceneCN: 这里 repay 指「偿还借款」（第 1 个义项：归还所欠的钱）；句意为他计划在两年内还清全部债务。图中可辨识物件：借条、转账记录、日历。

pos.zh: 偿还；报答（及物/不及物均可）

senses.title: to pay back money
senses.definition: to give back money that was borrowed or owed
senses.definitionCN: 把借来的或欠下的钱还给对方
senses.example: She repaid the loan three months early.
senses.exampleCN: 她提前三个月还清了贷款。
senses.why: This is the basic re- + pay sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是 re- + pay 的基本义。

senses.title: to settle a debt
senses.definition: to discharge or settle an amount owed, whether money or another obligation
senses.definitionCN: 结清所欠金额，无论金钱或其他义务
senses.example: He repaid his debt to society by serving three years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过服刑三年来偿还对社会的债务。
senses.why: The monetary sense extends to any obligation one owes.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义延伸到任何亏欠的义务。

senses.title: to give back for kindness
senses.definition: to do or give something nice in return for a favour or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 为答谢恩惠或善意而做或给予美好的事物
senses.example: She repaid his kindness with a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一份礼物来报答他的善意。
senses.why: 'Pay back' moves from money to gratitude.
senses.whyCN: pay back 从金钱走到了感激。

senses.title: to return with interest
senses.definition: to return more than was borrowed or received
senses.definitionCN: 返还的比借入或收到的多
senses.example: I'll repay your generosity with interest.
senses.exampleCN: 我会加倍报答你的慷慨。
senses.why: The idea of repaying interest extends to any generous return.
senses.whyCN: 偿还利息的想法延伸到任何慷慨的回报。

senses.title: to compensate for injury
senses.definition: to make up for a harm or injury done to someone
senses.definitionCN: 弥补对某人造成的伤害
senses.example: The family repaid the stranger's carelessness with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人对陌生人的粗心给予了愤怒的「回报」。
senses.why: Paying back an injury is the dark side of the repay idea.
senses.whyCN: 偿还伤害是 repay 想法的阴暗面。

senses.title: to equal a benefit
senses.definition: to be worth enough to make up for a cost or sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 价值足以弥补代价或牺牲
senses.example: The joys of teaching repay the long hours.
senses.exampleCN: 教书的乐趣足以回报那些漫长的工作时间。
senses.why: Abstract value makes up for cost, like a repayment.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的价值弥补代价，就像 repayment 一样。

senses.title: to refund
senses.definition: to give money back because of a return or cancellation
senses.definitionCN: 因退货或取消而把钱还给对方
senses.example: The shop repaid the full amount when the product broke.
senses.exampleCN: 产品损坏后商店全额退款。
senses.why: A refund is a kind of repayment for money received.
senses.whyCN: 退款是偿还已收金额的一种形式。

senses.title: to respond in kind
senses.definition: to respond to an action with a similar action
senses.definitionCN: 以类似的行动回应某个行动
senses.example: If he insults you, don't repay him in the same coin.
senses.exampleCN: 如果他骂你，不要以牙还牙。
senses.why: Paying back an action mirrors the structure of repaying money.
senses.whyCN: 偿还一个行为在结构上跟还钱一样。

intro.en: Repay is a transparent compound: re- 'back' + pay. Pay itself comes from Old French payer 'to appease', which comes from Latin pacare.
intro.cn: repay 是清晰的复合：re-「回」+ pay。pay 来自古法语 payer「安抚」，后者来自拉丁语 pacare。

items.en: Latin re- 'back, again' formed many Middle English compound verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁语 re-「回、再」在中古英语构成很多复合动词。

items.en: Old French payer came from Latin pacare 'to appease, make peace', built on pax 'peace'.
items.cn: 古法语 payer 来自拉丁语 pacare「使和平、安抚」，由 pax「和平」构成。

items.en: English pay entered around 1300 from Old French.
items.cn: 英语 pay 约 1300 年从古法语进入。

items.en: repay was formed by early Middle English (around 1300) as a transparent compound of re- + pay.
items.cn: repay 在早期中古英语（约 1300）由 re- + pay 构成，是清晰的复合。

items.en: The past tense and past participle repaid follows an irregular pattern: repay → repaid by analogy with pay → paid.
items.cn: 过去式和过去分词 repaid 按不规则形式：repay → repaid，类比 pay → paid。

items.en: All etymology solid; the 'appease' origin of pay is well established in historical lexicography.
items.cn: 全部词源可靠；pay「安抚」的起源在历史词典学中已充分确立。

note.en: Look-alikes share the pay root; near meanings are ways of giving something back.
note.cn: 形近共享 pay 词根；近义是把某物还给对方的各种方式。

definition_en: the ground on which a battle is fought, and by extension any area or sphere where a struggle takes place
core_image: 被车辙压出深沟的田野，断栅与散落的盔甲之间，远处两面破旗还立着
scene: 清晨的田野上留着深深的车辙与断栅，散落的盔甲被露水打湿，远处两面破旗仍插在土里。 The battlefield lay silent after the last regiment withdrew.
sceneCN: 这里 battlefield 指「两军实际交战的那片地面」（第 1 个义项：战斗发生的地点本身）；句意为最后一支团撤退之后，战场一片寂静。图中可辨识物件：车辙、断栅、散落盔甲、远处两面破旗。

pos.zh: 战场；交战地带；斗争领域（可数；复数 battlefields）

derivatives.zh: 战斗；搏斗（古法语 bataille < 拉丁 battualia「士兵的击打练习」< battuere「击打」，battuere 更深来源不确定）
战场；争夺之地（battle 加 ground，由「战斗」转为「战斗发生的地面」）
营；作战单位（法语 bataillon < 意大利 battaglione，与 battaglia「战斗」同族，由「战斗」转为「战斗编制」）
田野；领域；实地（古英语 feld「开阔地」，由「开阔地」转为「活动领域」）
守场员（field 加 -er，指在场上负责某一区域的人）
守备；实地操作（field 加 -ing，指在场上或实地进行的过程）

senses.title: The ground of a battle
senses.definition: the actual piece of ground on which opposing forces meet and fight
senses.definitionCN: 敌对双方相遇并交战的真实地面
senses.example: The battlefield lay silent after the last regiment withdrew.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一支团撤退之后，战场一片寂静。
senses.why: Battle names the fighting and field names the open ground, so the compound is simply the ground where the fighting happens.
senses.whyCN: battle 指战斗，field 指开阔地面，因此这个复合词就是战斗发生的那片地面。

senses.title: The wider zone of combat
senses.definition: the larger area around the fighting, including approaches, reserves and rear positions
senses.definitionCN: 战斗周边更大的区域，包括接近路线、预备队与后方阵地
senses.example: The whole valley became a battlefield once the artillery found the range.
senses.exampleCN: 炮兵测准距离之后，整条山谷都成了战场。
senses.why: A battle spreads outward through artillery and movement, so the word expands from the meeting point to the whole contested zone.
senses.whyCN: 战斗会通过炮火与机动向外扩散，因此这个词从相遇点扩展到整片争夺地带。

senses.title: The scene after the fighting
senses.definition: the field as it is found afterwards, marked by wreckage, graves and abandoned equipment
senses.definitionCN: 战后被人看到的场地，遍布残骸、坟墓与丢弃的装备
senses.example: Photographers walked the battlefield at dawn, counting the wrecked guns.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在黎明时走过战场，清点被毁的火炮。
senses.why: Once the noise stops, the ground becomes a scene to be inspected, and the same word names that aftermath.
senses.whyCN: 枪炮声停止之后，这片地面变成可供查看的现场，同一个词就指这种战后景象。

senses.title: A figurative arena of struggle
senses.definition: any sphere in which rivals contend, such as politics, science or the market
senses.definitionCN: 竞争对手相争的任何领域，如政治、科学或市场
senses.example: The courtroom became the battlefield for two rival laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭成了两家竞争实验室的战场。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essentials of the literal scene: two sides, a contested space and a result that is won or lost.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了字面场景的核心：两方、一片争夺的空间，以及一个分出胜负的结果。

senses.title: The electronic or cyber battlefield
senses.definition: the digital domain in which networks, signals and data are attacked and defended
senses.definitionCN: 对网络、信号与数据进行攻防的数字领域
senses.example: Engineers now map the cyber battlefield as carefully as any hill.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师如今像测绘任何一座山丘那样仔细地测绘网络战场。
senses.why: New domains inherit old words because the shape of attack, defence and terrain remains the same without soil.
senses.whyCN: 新领域会继承旧词，因为攻防与地形的结构在没有土壤时仍然相同。

senses.title: The negotiating table as a battlefield
senses.definition: a rhetorical use for a negotiation in which each concession is treated as ground gained or lost
senses.definitionCN: 修辞用法，指把每一次让步都视为得失地盘的谈判
senses.example: Both delegations treated the treaty talks as a battlefield of paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 两个代表团把条约谈判当成逐段争夺的战场。
senses.why: Negotiation has fronts, trenches and withdrawals in miniature, so speakers borrow the field to describe them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判以缩小的规模拥有前线、战壕与撤退，因此说话者借这片场地来描写它。

senses.title: A historic site and memorial
senses.titleCN: 作为历史遗址与纪念地
senses.definition: a preserved field visited for its monuments, graves and guided tours rather than for fighting
senses.definitionCN: 因纪念碑、墓地与导览而被参观的保存场地，而非用于作战
senses.example: The old battlefield is now a park with a visitors' centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这片旧战场如今是一座设有游客中心的公园。
senses.why: When the fighting is long past, the ground survives as a place of memory, and the word follows it into heritage.
senses.whyCN: 战斗久远之后，这片地面作为记忆之地留存下来，词义也随之进入遗产领域。

senses.title: The front line of hospitals or disasters
senses.titleCN: 医院或灾难中的前线比喻
senses.definition: a journalistic use for the place where medical staff or rescue workers face the heaviest pressure
senses.definitionCN: 新闻用法，指医护人员或救援人员承受最大压力的地方
senses.example: The emergency ward was the battlefield of the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 急诊病房是夜班的前线战场。
senses.why: The word transfers wherever people hold a line under pressure, and a ward or a flood zone has exactly that line.
senses.whyCN: 只要人们顶着压力守住一条线，这个词就能迁移过去，而病房或洪区正有这样一条线。

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived word for fighting to an Old English word for open land; the two halves are unrelated. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把一个源自拉丁语的「打斗」词与一个古英语的「开阔地」词连在一起，两半互不同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Battuere meant 'to beat, strike'; its deeper origin is source uncertain, and no earlier root is reliably attested.
items.cn: battuere 意为「击打、敲打」；其更深来源属来源不确定，没有可靠书证的更早词根。

items.en: Battualia named the striking exercises of soldiers, and from that practice the word came to mean a fight.
items.cn: battualia 指士兵的击打演练，由这种练习引申为一场打斗。

items.en: Old French bataille carried the sense of a battle into English, where it named the engagement itself.
items.cn: 古法语 bataille 把「战斗」的含义带入英语，指交战本身。

items.en: Feld meant open land, a wide flat stretch, and it is the source of the field half of the compound.
items.cn: feld 指开阔地、大片平地，是这个复合词中 field 一半的来源。

items.en: English joined battle and field into one noun for the ground of an engagement, and the compound has kept that literal core.
items.cn: 英语把 battle 与 field 合成一个指交战地面的名词，这个复合词一直保留这一字面核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first written use of the compound is not recorded, and the deeper origin of battuere is a matter of reconstruction rather than attested fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词确切的最早书证没有记载，battuere 的更深来源属于重构而非有书证的事实。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves and the near-doublet from the compound; group two holds terms for the spaces where fighting is organized.
note.cn: 第一组把这个复合词的两半及近义双式词分开；第二组是用于组织作战的空间名称。

entries.definition: A single engagement between armed forces; the field is only the place where it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指武装力量之间的一次交战；field 只是它发生的地点。

entries.definition: Open land or a sphere of activity; it need not be contested at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔地或活动领域；它完全不必是被争夺的。

entries.definition: Essentially the same ground as battlefield, but it is the more common choice in political and commercial metaphors.
entries.definitionCN: 本质上与 battlefield 指同一片地面，但在政治与商业比喻中更常用。

entries.definition: A military unit, from the same Italian battle family; it is an organization of soldiers, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个军事单位，同出意大利语「战斗」词族；它是士兵的编制，不是地点。

entries.definition: The whole geographic area in which a war is conducted; a battlefield is one small part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行一场战争的整个地理区域；battlefield 只是其中很小的一部分。

entries.definition: The moving line where opposing forces meet; it is a boundary, while a battlefield is an area.
entries.definitionCN: 指敌对力量相遇的移动界线；它是一条线，而 battlefield 是一片区域。

entries.definition: An area officially designated as dangerous because of fighting; the term is administrative as much as military.
entries.definitionCN: 指因交战而被正式划为危险的区域；这个词既是军事用语，也是行政用语。

entries.definition: A place or sphere of contest, from Latin arena 'sand'; it matches the figurative battlefield, not the literal one.
entries.definitionCN: 指较量之处或领域，出自拉丁 arena「沙」；它对应比喻性的 battlefield，而非字面战场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Battle plus field is transparent: the fighting plus the open ground it happens on.
normal.cn: battle 加 field 结构透明：战斗加上它发生的开阔地面。

normal.en: The battle family runs battuere, battualia, bataille, battle, battalion, battleground.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 battuere、battualia、bataille、battle、battalion、battleground。

normal.en: The field half is Old English feld 'open land', the same word that survives in field and fielder.
normal.cn: field 一半是古英语 feld「开阔地」，同一词还留在 field 与 fielder 中。

normal.en: Collocations mark the literal and the figurative: on the battlefield, battlefield medicine, the battlefield of ideas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出字面与比喻：在战场上、战地医疗、思想战场。

normal.en: Two halves, two origins: battle is Latin through French, field is Old English, and they only met in English.
normal.cn: 两半两个来源：battle 经法语来自拉丁语，field 是古英语，二者只在英语中相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a ploughed field cut by a single deep line of wheel ruts.
abstract.cn: 想象一片耕过的田野被一道深深的车辙切开。

abstract.en: Picture two broken flags leaning toward each other across empty ground.
abstract.cn: 想象两面破旗隔着空地相互倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a chessboard where every square is a hill that someone must take.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棋盘，每一格都是必须有人攻占的山丘。

examples.en: Medics carried the wounded off the battlefield under fire.
examples.cn: 医护兵在炮火下把伤员抬离战场。

examples.en: The novel turns the family kitchen into a battlefield of small quarrels.
examples.cn: 这部小说把家里的厨房变成小争吵的战场。

examples.en: Researchers treat the deep sea as the next battlefield for mining rights.
examples.cn: 研究者把深海视为采矿权争夺的下一个战场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「battle（打）+ field（地）」——打起来的那片地 → 战场

root: 战斗：battle < 古法语 bataille < 拉丁 battualia「士兵的击打练习」< battuere「击打」，battuere 更深来源属来源不确定。地面：field < 古英语 feld「开阔地」。两半不同源，只在英语中合为复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one field: the ground of the fight widens into a zone, becomes an aftermath, then serves as a metaphor for any contest, a cyber domain, a negotiating table, a heritage site and finally a hospital front line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片地面铺开：交战的地面扩成地带，变成战后现场，再被借作任何较量的比喻、网络领域、谈判桌、历史遗址，最后是医院前线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rutted field where two sides met, still carrying the marks of the encounter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片布满车辙的田野，两方曾在此相遇，地上仍留着交手的痕迹。

branches.en: POINT AND ZONE: the meeting ground and the wider contested area are the same field at two scales.
branches.cn: 交点与地带：相遇的地面与更广的争夺区域，是同一片场地在两种尺度上的样子。

branches.en: AFTERMATH AND METAPHOR: what is found afterwards becomes the image for any struggle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 现场与比喻：战后所见的景象，变成别处任何斗争的形象。

branches.en: NEW DOMAINS: networks and negotiating tables inherit the field because attack and defence keep their shape.
branches.cn: 新领域：网络与谈判桌继承了这片场地，因为攻与守的结构不变。

branches.en: HERITAGE: the fighting ends, and the ground survives as a place to visit and remember.
branches.cn: 遗产：战斗结束，这片地面作为可参观、可记忆之处留存下来。

branches.en: FRONT LINE: wards and flood zones repeat the literal line under pressure.
branches.cn: 前线：病房与洪区在压力下重演了那条字面意义的线。

intro.en: The compound is made of two unrelated pieces: a Latin-derived battle word and an Old English field word.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个互不相关的部分组成：一个源自拉丁语的「战斗」词，和一个古英语的「田野」词。

latinIntro.en: Battuere and battualia are the attested Latin ancestors of battle; field has no Latin ancestor and comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: battuere 与 battualia 是 battle 有书证的拉丁祖先；field 没有拉丁祖先，来自古英语。

items.structure: battuere, battui, battutum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the physical blow behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为整族词提供了物理上的击打动作。

items.example: The practice ground turns into the word for a fight.
items.exampleCN: 练习的场地转为表示一场打斗的词。

items.structure: bataille (Old French noun, from Latin battualia)
items.example: Old French carries the Latin word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个拉丁词带入英语。

items.structure: battle (English noun, from Old French bataille)
items.example: The noun names the event, not the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名的是事件，而不是地点。

items.example: The Old English word names wide ground with no trees.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语词指没有树木的宽阔地面。

items.structure: field (English noun, from Old English feld)
items.meaning: open ground; an area of activity
items.example: The word widens from soil to any sphere of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从土地扩展到任何工作领域。

items.example: The compound is literal before it is metaphorical.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词先有字面义，后有比喻义。

items.example: The variant swaps the field word for a more general ground word.
items.exampleCN: 这个变体把 field 换成更一般的 ground。

items.example: The suffix yields fielder from field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 field 造出 fielder。

items.example: The suffix yields fielding, work done in the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出 fielding，即在场地上进行的工作。

definition_zh: 不溶的；不能溶解的；（问题、矛盾）无法解决的
definition_en: not able to be dissolved in a liquid, or not able to be solved or settled
core_image: 一勺细粉落进水里，沉到底部，搅了很久仍是清清楚楚的一层
scene: 水槽里，工人把一袋白色粉末倒进清水，粉末沉到槽底，怎么搅也不散开。 The powder stayed insoluble no matter how long the water was stirred.
sceneCN: 这里 insoluble 指物质不能在液体中溶解（第 1 个义项：不能溶于液体）；句意为无论搅多久，这种粉末都不溶解。图中可辨识物件：水槽、白色粉末、搅拌棒、沉底的粉层。

pos.zh: 不溶的；不能溶解的
（问题、矛盾）无法解决的；不能化解的

senses.title: Will not dissolve in a liquid
senses.definition: not capable of being dissolved in a liquid, so that the substance stays separate and visible
senses.definitionCN: 不能溶解于液体，物质保持分离、看得见
senses.example: The oil remained insoluble in water and floated on top.
senses.exampleCN: 油不溶于水，浮在上面。
senses.why: the negative prefix in- reverses soluble, so the word denies the loosening of particles that soluble describes.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 反转 soluble，这个词否认了 soluble 所描述的微粒散开。

senses.title: Insoluble in a named solvent
senses.definition: failing to dissolve in the particular liquid that is named, even though it may dissolve elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在被点名的液体中不溶解，尽管在别处可能溶解
senses.example: This pigment is insoluble in alcohol but soluble in acetone.
senses.exampleCN: 这种颜料不溶于酒精，却溶于丙酮。
senses.why: since dissolving is a relation between two substances, a refusal is also a relation and needs the solvent named.
senses.whyCN: 既然溶解是两物之间的关系，拒绝溶解也是一种关系，同样需要点明溶剂。

senses.title: A solid that stays as residue
senses.titleCN: 沉淀下来的不溶固体或残渣
senses.definition: remaining as a solid residue after a liquid has been filtered or poured off
senses.definitionCN: 液体被滤过或倒掉后仍留成固体残渣
senses.example: The insoluble residue was collected on the filter paper.
senses.exampleCN: 不溶残渣被收集在滤纸上。
senses.why: what cannot dissolve must end up somewhere, and in the laboratory it ends up as the residue on the paper.
senses.whyCN: 不能溶解的东西总得有个去处，在实验室里它就成了纸上的残渣。

senses.title: A problem with no apparent answer
senses.definition: unable to be solved or settled, said of a difficulty that resists every proposed remedy
senses.definitionCN: 无法解决或了结，指抵挡一切方案的那种困难
senses.example: The housing shortage seemed insoluble without new land.
senses.exampleCN: 没有新土地，住房短缺似乎无解。
senses.why: the mind unties problems as a liquid unties salts, so a problem that will not come apart is called insoluble.
senses.whyCN: 头脑解问题正如液体解盐，解不开的问题就被叫作 insoluble。

senses.title: A dispute that cannot be reconciled
senses.definition: unable to be brought into agreement, said of opposed claims or interests
senses.definitionCN: 无法使之一致，指对立的主张或利益
senses.example: Their claims were insoluble because both demanded the same field.
senses.exampleCN: 两方都索要同一块地，他们的主张无法调和。
senses.why: two positions that cannot be untied remain locked, which is exactly the image behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 两个解不开的立场会一直互锁，这正是这个词背后的画面。

senses.title: A mystery that cannot be explained
senses.definition: unable to be explained or accounted for, said of a disappearance, a riddle or an event
senses.definitionCN: 无法被解释或说明，指失踪、谜语或某个事件
senses.example: The disappearance remained insoluble for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 那起失踪案数十年没有答案。
senses.why: a riddle is a knot in thought; if no clue loosens it, the knot stays insoluble.
senses.whyCN: 谜语是思路上的结，若没有线索能松开它，这个结就始终解不开。

senses.title: A debt that cannot be discharged
senses.definition: unable to be paid off or discharged, used of an obligation that no arrangement can clear
senses.definitionCN: 无法还清或了结，用于任何安排都清不掉的义务
senses.example: The old debt proved insoluble and was written off.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔旧债无法清偿，最终被注销。
senses.why: a debt is a bond, and to discharge it is to untie it; a bond that cannot be untied is insoluble in the older legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 债务是一种束缚，清偿就是解开；解不开的束缚在旧日法律意义上就是 insoluble。

senses.title: A knot that cannot be untied, an old use
senses.definition: unable to be undone, said of a knot, a band or a fastening in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中指绳结、束带或系缚无法解开
senses.example: The insoluble knot had to be cut with a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 那个死结只能用刀割开。
senses.why: the physical knot is the oldest sense, and every later use keeps the same image of a bond that will not loosen.
senses.whyCN: 实体的绳结是最古老的义项，此后每个用法都保留「束缚不肯松开」这一意象。

intro.en: Insoluble joins the negative prefix in- 'not' to soluble, from Latin insolubilis 'that cannot be loosened or dissolved'. The word is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with the figurative sense of an unanswerable problem following in the sixteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: insoluble 由否定前缀 in-「不」加 soluble 构成，来自拉丁 insolubilis「不能松开或溶解的」。英语自十四世纪有记录，十六世纪出现「问题无解」的比喻义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere 'to loosen, untie, dissolve' is built from se- 'apart' and luere 'to loosen'; the same verb yields solve, solution and dissolve.
items.cn: solvere「松开、解开、溶解」由 se-「分开」与 luere「松开」构成，同一动词衍生 solve、solution 与 dissolve。

items.en: In- 'not' plus solubilis 'able to be dissolved' produced insolubilis, used of knots that would not come undone as well as of substances that would not dissolve.
items.cn: in-「不」加 solubilis「可被溶解的」构成 insolubilis，既用于解不开的绳结，也用于不能溶解的物质。

items.en: Old French insoluble brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, at first almost entirely in the physical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 insoluble 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初几乎全是实体义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century chemistry made the word a standard label for solids that a solvent leaves untouched, and the laboratory phrase insoluble residue dates from this period.
items.cn: 十七世纪的化学把这个词变成溶剂动不了的固体的标准标签，实验室里把这类残渣称为「不溶残渣」，这一说法即出自这一时期。

items.en: By the sixteenth century insoluble was applied to problems and disputes that no remedy could settle, borrowing the chemical image for the mind.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，insoluble 被用于任何办法都了结不了的问题与争端，把化学意象借给了头脑。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first citation): the pre-Latin form of luere is a reconstruction, and no exact date is recorded for the first English use of the figurative sense.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见书证）：luere 在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构，比喻义在英语中最早使用的确切年代没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds the negative forms that look interchangeable but answer different questions; group two holds words for things that resist solution or passage.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来可互换、实际回答不同问题的否定形式；第二组是表示抗拒溶解或通过之物的词。

entries.definition: The exact opposite in the chemical sense; it also carries the sense of a solvable problem, which insoluble mirrors.
entries.definitionCN: 化学义上完全相反；它也带「问题可解」义，insoluble 与之对应。

entries.definition: A plain English negative used only for problems and puzzles, with no chemical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 纯英语否定形式，只用于问题与谜题，完全没有化学义。

entries.definition: A separate adjective meaning 'not solvable', built on solvable rather than on soluble; it never describes a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个形容词，意为「不可解」，由 solvable 而非 soluble 构成；从不形容物质。

entries.definition: Built on dissolve: it describes ties, vows or unions that cannot be broken, not salts that will not dissolve.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dissolve 构成：描述无法解除的联系、誓言或结合，而非不溶解的盐。

entries.definition: Describes a problem or person that is hard to manage, but not necessarily impossible; insoluble is stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容难以处理的问题或人，但未必不可能；insoluble 语气更强。

entries.definition: Describes a barrier that fluid cannot pass through; it is about passage, not about dissolving.
entries.definitionCN: 形容流体无法穿过的屏障；说的是通过，不是溶解。

entries.definition: Used of conflicts or doubts that cannot be resolved, close to the dispute sense of insoluble.
entries.definitionCN: 用于无法化解的冲突或疑虑，接近 insoluble 的争端义。

entries.definition: An everyday adjective for something that will not give way, used of people, stains and problems alike.
entries.definitionCN: 日常形容词，指不肯让步之物，可用于人、污渍与问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: In- 'not' on top of soluble: the loosening is denied.
normal.cn: in-「不」加在 soluble 之上：拒绝松开。

normal.en: The pair runs soluble and insoluble, solubility and insolubility.
normal.cn: 成对出现的是 soluble 与 insoluble、solubility 与 insolubility。

normal.en: Laboratory phrases mark the solid sense: insoluble residue, insoluble salt.
normal.cn: 实验室说法标出实体义：不溶残渣、难溶盐。

normal.en: Everyday phrases mark the figurative sense: an insoluble problem, an insoluble conflict.
normal.cn: 日常说法标出比喻义：无解的问题、无法调和的冲突。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with insolvable, which is built on solvable and applies only to questions.
normal.cn: 不要与 insolvable 混同，后者由 solvable 构成，只用于问题。

abstract.en: Picture powder that keeps its shape on the bottom of a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象粉末在杯底始终保持着原来的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a knot pulled tight until no finger can find a loop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被拉到最紧，手指再也找不到可以插入的环。

abstract.en: Picture two negotiators holding the same map and refusing to move their pens.
abstract.cn: 想象两位谈判者拿着同一张地图，谁也不肯挪笔。

examples.en: Calcium carbonate is insoluble in water but reacts with acid.
examples.cn: 碳酸钙不溶于水，但会与酸反应。

examples.en: The report called the shortage of trained nurses an insoluble problem.
examples.cn: 报告称训练有素的护士短缺是一个无法解决的问题。

examples.en: The two communities held insoluble claims to the same water source.
examples.cn: 两个社区对同一水源的主张无法调和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（不）+ soluble（可溶）」——不溶的；再引申为「解不开的」

root: 拉丁 insolubilis「不能松开、不能溶解的」= in-（不）+ solubilis（可被溶解的）；solubilis 出自 solvere（松开、解开），由 se-（分开）+ luere（松开）构成。英语经古法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one refusal to loosen: powder stays on the bottom, a named solvent gets no answer, residue remains on the paper, a problem and a dispute will not untie, a mystery keeps its secret, a debt cannot be discharged, and finally an old knot has to be cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「拒绝松开」：粉末留在杯底，指定溶剂得不到回应，残渣留在滤纸上，问题与争端解不开，谜团守着秘密，债务清不掉，最后是一个旧绳结只能用刀割断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid that stays whole on the bottom while the liquid moves around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：固体完完整整留在底部，液体在它周围流动。

branches.en: REFUSED DISSOLVING: the bare denial and the solvent-specific denial are one refusal seen twice.
branches.cn: 拒绝溶解：笼统的否定与对指定溶剂的否定，是同一次拒绝的两种看法。

branches.en: RESIDUE: what will not dissolve has to remain somewhere, and the laboratory makes that place visible.
branches.cn: 残渣：不溶之物总得留在某处，实验室让这个去处看得见。

branches.en: LOCKED IN THE MIND: a problem and a dispute are knots no remedy can loosen.
branches.cn: 锁在脑中：问题与争端都是任何办法也松不开的结。

branches.en: UNEXPLAINED AND UNPAID: a mystery keeps its secret and a debt keeps its bond.
branches.cn: 无法解释与无法清偿：谜团守着秘密，债务守着束缚。

branches.en: THE OLDEST KNOT: the physical knot that must be cut is the root image of every later sense.
branches.cn: 最古老的结：只能用刀割断的实体绳结，是此后一切义项的根源意象。

intro.en: Insoluble is a negative built on a Latin adjective, and both the negative prefix and the Latin base also build other common words.
intro.cn: insoluble 是在一个拉丁形容词上构成的否定词，否定前缀与拉丁词基都还构成其他常用词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix in- 'not' appears as il-, im- and ir- before other consonants; Latin solvere 'to loosen' supplies solution, dissolve and absolute.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀 in- 在其他辅音前会变成 il-、im- 与 ir-；拉丁 solvere「松开」提供 solution、dissolve 与 absolute。

items.example: The prefix turns the positive adjective into its denial.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把肯定形容词变成它的否定。

items.meaning: not, before a word beginning with l
items.meaningCN: 不（用于以 l 开头的词前）
items.example: The same prefix appears as il- in illegal.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀在 illegal 中写作 il-。

items.structure: im- (form of in- before m, b, p)
items.example: The variant appears in impermeable.
items.exampleCN: 这一变体出现在 impermeable 中。

items.example: The verb supplies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族。

items.example: The base adjective names a capacity.
items.exampleCN: 基础形容词命名的是一种能力。

items.example: The powder is insoluble in water.
items.exampleCN: 这种粉末不溶于水。

items.example: Its insolubility limits its use in drinks.
items.exampleCN: 它的不可溶性限制了它在饮料中的用途。

items.example: Sugar is soluble in water.
items.exampleCN: 糖溶于水。

items.example: The solution was filtered twice.
items.exampleCN: 这溶液被过滤了两次。

items.meaning: to break apart in a liquid
items.example: Salt dissolves quickly in hot water.
items.exampleCN: 盐在热水中很快溶解。

latinEntries.meaning: that cannot be loosened or dissolved
the quality of not being dissolvable

definition_zh: 宏观经济学；研究整体经济的产出、就业、物价与增长的经济学分支
definition_en: the branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, especially total output, employment, price levels and growth
core_image: 一张从高空拍下的城市照片，港口、工厂与公路被压缩成几条并排的总量曲线
scene: 央行与财政部门的官员围坐一桌，争论的是全国产出、失业与物价的整体走向。 Macroeconomics asks why total output and employment rise and fall together over the business cycle.
sceneCN: 央行与财政官员围坐一桌，争论全国产出、失业与物价的整体走向；句中的 macroeconomics 指「把整个经济当作一个总量单位来研究的分支」（第 1 个义项：研究整体经济运行的学科）。图中可辨识物件：总量曲线、城市航拍图、会议桌、报表。

pos.zh: 宏观经济学；总量经济学

derivatives.zh: 宏观经济的；总量经济的

senses.title: The branch studying the whole economy
senses.titleCN: 研究整体经济的学科分支
senses.definition: the division of economics that treats the economy as a single system rather than as separate markets
senses.definitionCN: 把经济当作一个单一体系、而非若干独立市场来研究的经济学分支
senses.example: Macroeconomics examines how investment and consumption move together.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学考察投资与消费如何同步变动。
senses.why: The prefix marks scale, and the base names the discipline, so the compound literally means the study of the economy at its largest scale.
senses.whyCN: 前缀标记尺度，基础词指学科，因此这个复合词字面上就是「在最大尺度上研究经济」。

senses.title: The university subject
senses.definition: the name of a standard course and textbook in a degree programme
senses.definitionCN: 学位课程中一门标准课程与教材的名称
senses.example: She took macroeconomics before moving on to monetary policy.
senses.exampleCN: 她先修宏观经济学，之后才转向货币政策。
senses.why: A discipline that is taught in set courses turns its branch names into subject titles, and this one is among the earliest in any programme.
senses.whyCN: 学科若按固定课程讲授，分支之名便成为科目名称，而这个分支是任何培养方案里最早的科目之一。

senses.title: The aggregate viewpoint
senses.definition: the habit of looking at totals and averages instead of at individual buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 看总量与平均值、而非单个买卖双方的习惯视角
senses.example: Macroeconomics smooths away individual choices to show the total picture.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学把个体选择抹平，以呈现总体图景。
senses.why: The word's scale prefix sets it against the small-scale branch, so using it signals that the unit of analysis is a total, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词表示尺度的前缀使它与小尺度分支相对，因此使用它就表明分析单位是总量而非个人。

senses.title: Analysis for fiscal and monetary policy
senses.titleCN: 为财政与货币政策服务的分析
senses.definition: the applied use of totals to decide on spending, taxation and interest rates
senses.definitionCN: 把总量分析用于决定支出、税收与利率的应用做法
senses.example: The treasury relied on macroeconomics to size the stimulus.
senses.exampleCN: 财政部依靠宏观经济学来确定刺激方案的规模。
senses.why: Governments act on totals, so the branch that supplies totals became the natural language of budget and rate decisions.
senses.whyCN: 政府依据总量行动，因此提供总量的分支自然成为预算与利率决策的语言。

senses.title: Short-run fluctuation
senses.definition: the study of booms and recessions over months and a few years
senses.definitionCN: 研究数月到数年之间的繁荣与衰退
senses.example: Macroeconomics explains why recessions spread from one sector to all.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学解释衰退为何从一个部门扩散到所有部门。
senses.why: When totals are measured quarterly, their short swings become visible, and the branch took that rhythm as one of its central problems.
senses.whyCN: 总量一旦按季度计量，短期摆动便显现出来，这个分支便把这种节奏当作核心问题之一。

senses.title: Long-run growth
senses.definition: the study of why output per person rises over decades
senses.definitionCN: 研究数十年间人均产出为何提高
senses.example: Macroeconomics now devotes much of its attention to productivity growth.
senses.exampleCN: 宏观经济学如今把大量注意力放在生产率增长上。
senses.why: The same totals, viewed across decades rather than quarters, raise the separate question of growth, which the branch treats as its long horizon.
senses.whyCN: 同样一些总量若按数十年而非季度来看，便提出增长这一独立问题，这个分支把它当作长期视野。

senses.title: The open economy
senses.titleCN: 开放经济中的宏观分析
senses.definition: the study of totals when trade, exchange rates and capital cross borders
senses.definitionCN: 在贸易、汇率与资本跨越国界时研究总量
senses.example: Macroeconomics of the open economy tracks the trade balance alongside growth.
senses.exampleCN: 开放经济的宏观经济学把贸易差额与增长一并追踪。
senses.why: Once national totals are measured against other countries, the branch must add exchange rates and cross-border flows to its core accounts.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国民总量要与他国比较，这个分支就必须在核心核算中加入汇率与跨境流动。

senses.title: Loose talk about the big picture
senses.titleCN: 口语引申：从整体层面看问题
senses.definition: in informal use, the habit of judging a local event by its effect on the whole system
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指以整体体系所受影响来判断局部事件的习惯
senses.example: Treating the plant closure as macroeconomics, the mayor asked what it did to the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 市长把工厂关闭当作宏观层面的问题，追问它给整个城镇带来了什么。
senses.why: Because the term's core is the whole rather than the part, it can be borrowed for any decision that must be judged at the level of the system.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个术语的核心是整体而非局部，它可以被借用来描述任何必须在体系层面判断的决定。

intro.en: Macroeconomics joins a Greek prefix meaning 'long, large' to economics, which descends from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia. The compound and its adjective are generally thought to have risen in the 1930s with national income accounting and Keynesian aggregate analysis; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个表示「长的、大的」的希腊前缀加在经济学科之名上，而后者经拉丁 oeconomia 源自希腊 oikonomia。一般认为这个复合词及其形容词形式在二十世纪三十年代随国民收入核算与凯恩斯式总量分析兴起；具体首见年份来源不确定。

items.en: Makros meant 'long, large, far-reaching' and was widely used in compounds for things on a great scale.
items.cn: makros 意为「长的、大的、范围广的」，广泛用于表示大尺度的复合词。

items.en: Oikonomia, from oikos 'household' and nemein 'to manage', named the running of a household and later of public affairs.
items.cn: oikonomia 由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「管理」构成，指经营家宅，后也指管理公共事务。

items.en: Latin oeconomia carried the word into European learned usage, where it covered the management of an estate or a state.
items.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 把这个词带入欧洲学术用语，其范围包括庄园或国家的管理。

items.en: In the nineteenth century political economy was shortened to economics, giving the base that the large-scale prefix would later attach to.
items.cn: 十九世纪政治经济学缩称为经济学，为后来加接大尺度前缀提供了基础词。

items.en: The adjective is generally thought to have appeared in the 1930s, when economists needed a word for analysis of totals rather than of single markets.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词在二十世纪三十年代出现，当时经济学家需要为「分析总量而非单个市场」造一个词。

items.en: The noun settled as the name of a branch in the same decade, alongside national income accounts and aggregate demand analysis; the first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 同一时期，这个名词固定为一个分支的名称，与国民收入核算和总需求分析相伴；最早见于记载的年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms from the same compound that differ in word class or scale; the near-meaning group holds neighbouring fields that also work with totals but answer different questions.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一复合词中词性或尺度不同的形式；近义组收的是同样处理总量、但回答不同问题的邻近领域。

entries.definition: Describes totals or the branch itself, as in macroeconomic policy; it cannot stand alone as the name of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 描述总量或该分支本身，如宏观经济政策；它不能单独用作课程名称。

entries.definition: Studies single buyers, sellers and markets; the two words share their ending and are constantly paired and confused.
entries.definitionCN: 研究单个买方、卖方与市场；两词词尾相同，常被成对使用也常被混淆。

entries.definition: The whole subject, of which the large-scale branch is one part; it is broader, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 整个学科，大尺度分支只是其中一部分；它范围更广，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Names the whole economy as an object; it is what the branch studies, not the study itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为研究对象的整体经济；它是该分支研究的对象，而不是研究本身。

entries.definition: The measurement of total output, income and spending; it supplies the data that the branch interprets.
entries.definitionCN: 对总产出、总收入与总支出的计量；它提供该分支所解读的数据。

entries.definition: A narrower study of expansions and contractions; it is one part of the larger branch, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对扩张与收缩的更窄研究；它是该分支的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: Studies money, banking and interest rates; it overlaps with the branch but centres on one mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究货币、银行与利率；它与该分支重叠，却以一个机制为中心。

entries.definition: Explains why output per person rises over decades; it is the long-run wing of the branch.
entries.definitionCN: 解释数十年间人均产出为何提高；它是该分支的长期一翼。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here use the real Greek scale prefix, the real household root behind economics, and the real institutional setting in which the term grew up.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自表示尺度的真实希腊前缀、经济学背后真实的治家词根，以及这个术语成长的真实制度背景。

normal.en: Makros means long or large, so the prefix marks the scale of the whole economy.
normal.cn: makros 意为长或大，因此这个前缀标记的是整个经济的尺度。

normal.en: Oikonomia, household management, is the same root that gave economics.
normal.cn: oikonomia 即治家之术，正是给经济学提供词根的那个词。

normal.en: The field grew with national income accounting, which first made totals measurable.
normal.cn: 这门分支随国民收入核算成长，后者第一次让总量可以被计量。

normal.en: The pair with microeconomics is built into the word: large scale against small scale.
normal.cn: 它与微观经济学的配对就写在这个词里：大尺度对小尺度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the teaching sense: intermediate macroeconomics, applied macroeconomics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出教学义：中级宏观经济学、应用宏观经济学。

abstract.en: Picture an aerial photograph in which a whole city becomes a few clean lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张航拍照片，整座城市被压缩成几条干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture three curves, output, jobs and prices, drawn on one board and read together.
abstract.cn: 想象一块板子上画着产出、就业与物价三条曲线，被一起解读。

abstract.en: Picture one lever in a control room that is said to move every household at once.
abstract.cn: 想象控制室里的一根拉杆，据说能同时牵动每一个家庭。

examples.en: Macroeconomics is usually taught after students have learned how single markets work.
examples.cn: 宏观经济学通常在学生了解单个市场如何运行之后才讲授。

examples.en: The central bank's forecasts are grounded in macroeconomics rather than in firm-level data.
examples.cn: 央行的预测依据的是宏观经济学，而不是企业层面的数据。

examples.en: A recession is the kind of event that macroeconomics was invented to explain.
examples.cn: 衰退正是宏观经济学被创立出来要解释的那类事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「麦克罗伊科诺米克斯」：麦克罗先生只翻全国的厚账本，看的是整体的大数，不是一家小店的流水。

root: 希腊 makros「长的、大的」+ 希腊 oikonomia（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「管理」）→ 拉丁 oeconomia → 英语中的经济学；再加表示「大」的前缀构成宏观经济学，一般认为二十世纪三十年代随国民收入核算与总量分析定型，首见年份来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: the branch is named, taught, defined by its aggregate viewpoint, applied to policy, divided into short swings and long growth, widened to open economies, and finally borrowed in speech for any whole-system view.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：先给分支命名，再进入课堂，以总量视角界定自身，用于政策，分为短期波动与长期增长，扩展到开放经济，最后被口语借去指任何整体层面的看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one dashboard where the whole country's output, jobs and prices are read as a single instrument.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块仪表盘，全国的产出、就业与物价被当作同一台仪器来读。

branches.en: NAMING AND TEACHING: the branch is defined by its whole-economy object, then fixed as a standard course and textbook.
branches.cn: 命名与教学：该分支以整体经济为对象而被界定，随后固定为标准课程与教材。

branches.en: VIEWPOINT AND USE: looking at totals rather than individuals, and turning those totals into budget and rate decisions.
branches.cn: 视角与用途：看总量而非个体，再把总量变成预算与利率决策。

branches.en: TIME SCALES: quarterly swings of boom and slump, and the decades-long rise of output per person.
branches.cn: 时间尺度：季度性的繁荣与衰退摆动，以及数十年的人均产出增长。

branches.en: BORDERS: exchange rates, trade balances and capital flows enter the same accounts.
branches.cn: 国界：汇率、贸易差额与资本流动进入同一套核算。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the term escapes the classroom and names any judgment made at the level of the whole.
branches.cn: 被借用的尺度：这个术语走出课堂，用来指任何在整体层面作出的判断。

intro.en: The word is a prefix plus a discipline noun: a Greek element of size in front, and the household-derived name of economics behind.
intro.cn: 这个词是「前缀加学科名词」：前面是表示尺度的希腊成分，后面是由治家一词演变来的经济学之名。

latinIntro.en: Latin oeconomia and oeconomicus provide the older European forms of the economics half, while the size element was latinised as a combining form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 与 oeconomicus 提供「经济学」那一半较早的欧洲形式，而表示尺度的成分则被拉丁化为组合形式。

items.structure: prefix of Greek origin meaning large or long
items.meaning: at a large scale, taken as a whole
items.example: The prefix marks the whole economy as the unit of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把整个经济标记为研究单位。

items.example: Makros supplied the size element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: makros 提供了这个复合词中表示尺度的成分。

items.structure: Greek compound noun, oikos plus nemein
items.example: Oikonomia is the oldest layer of the base word.
items.exampleCN: oikonomia 是基础词最古老的一层。

items.meaning: management of an estate or state
items.example: Oeconomia carried the idea into learned Latin.
items.exampleCN: oeconomia 把这个观念带入学术拉丁语。

items.meaning: the study of production, trade and resources
items.meaningCN: 研究生产、贸易与资源的学科
items.example: Economics is the base to which the size prefix is added.
items.exampleCN: 经济学是加接尺度前缀的基础词。

items.structure: suffix naming a field of study
items.example: The suffix makes a subject name out of a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成学科名称。

items.meaning: relating to the economy as a whole
items.example: Macroeconomic data cover national totals.
items.exampleCN: 宏观数据涵盖国民总量。

items.meaning: a specialist in the whole-economy branch
items.example: A macroeconomist reads national accounts first.
items.exampleCN: 宏观经济学家最先读的是国民账户。

items.structure: prefix of Greek origin meaning small
items.meaning: at a small scale, one unit at a time
items.example: The opposite prefix names the smaller unit of study.
items.exampleCN: 相对的前缀命名更小的研究单位。

items.meaningCN: 研究整体经济总量的学科
items.example: Macroeconomics grew beside national income accounts.
items.exampleCN: 宏观经济学与国民收入核算一同成长。

latinEntries.meaning: management of a household or state

latinEntries.structure: oeconomicus, oeconomica, oeconomicum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 微观经济的；研究单个企业、住户或单个市场层面的
definition_en: relating to the choices of single firms, households or single markets rather than to the economy as a whole
core_image: 俯身看一间小店的账本：一位店主、一栏进货、一栏售价，视线只落在这一个柜台
scene: 一条街上开着许多小店，研究者却只盯住其中一家的账本。 The course begins with microeconomic choices made by a single household and a single firm.
sceneCN: 前半情境：一条街上许多小店，研究者只盯住其中一家的账本；句中的 microeconomic 指「以单个住户或单个企业为观察单位的」（第 1 个义项：研究单个主体而非全国总量）。图中可辨识物件：小店账本、价目牌、进货清单、算盘。

pos.zh: 微观经济的；单个主体层面的

derivatives.zh: 微观的；单个主体层面的

senses.title: Measured at the single unit
senses.definition: relating to one firm, one household or one producer rather than to totals for a whole country
senses.definitionCN: 与单个企业、单个住户或单个生产者相关，而非整个国家的总量
senses.example: Each microeconomic decision about hiring stays with the owner of the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个关于雇人的微观经济决定都由店主自己作出。
senses.why: the prefix for 'small' is attached to economic, so the adjective marks the unit observed: one agent, not the aggregate.
senses.whyCN: 表示「小」的前缀加在「经济的」之上，这个形容词因而标出观察的单位：一个主体，而非总量。

senses.title: Concentrated on one market
senses.definition: relating to a single market in which one good or service is bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 与买卖某一种商品或服务的单个市场相关
senses.example: The microeconomic question is why the price of one good rose.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的微观经济问题是：某一种商品的价格为何上涨。
senses.why: a single market is the smallest arena where supply meets demand, and the word marks that arena.
senses.whyCN: 单个市场是供给与需求相遇的最小场所，这个词标出的正是这个场所。

senses.title: Explaining individual choice
senses.definition: concerning the incentives and choices of individual buyers, workers or sellers
senses.definitionCN: 关于个体买方、劳动者或卖方的激励与选择
senses.example: Microeconomic reasoning explains why a consumer switches brands.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济推理能解释消费者为何更换品牌。
senses.why: once the unit is a person or a firm, the question becomes what that unit chooses and why.
senses.whyCN: 一旦单位落到一个人或一家企业，问题就变成这个单位选择什么、为什么选择。

senses.title: Analysing one relation at a time
senses.titleCN: 一次只分析一重关系的
senses.definition: using partial analysis, in which one relationship is examined while everything else is held unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 采用局部分析，在其余条件不变时考察一重关系
senses.example: A microeconomic treatment isolates the effect of a single tax.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济的处理方式把单一税种的影响单独分离出来。
senses.why: the method follows the unit: to see how one price responds, the analyst must keep the rest of the system still.
senses.whyCN: 方法跟单位走：要看清一个价格如何反应，分析者必须让系统的其余部分静止。

senses.title: Applied to a single industry
senses.definition: concerning the rules or performance of one industry or one sector rather than of the whole economy
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一个行业或某一个部门的规则或表现，而非整个经济
senses.example: Rules on one chain of stores are a microeconomic matter.
senses.exampleCN: 针对某一家连锁店的规则属于微观经济事项。
senses.why: an industry is a collection of units of the same kind, so policy aimed at it stays inside the word's scale.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业是同类单位的集合，针对它的政策仍在这个词的尺度之内。

senses.title: Built on disaggregated data
senses.titleCN: 基于分解到个体的数据的
senses.definition: based on data collected from separate units, such as individual households or individual plants
senses.definitionCN: 基于从各个独立单位收集的数据，如单个住户或单个工厂
senses.example: The survey provides microeconomic data on household spending.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查提供关于住户支出的微观经济数据。
senses.why: counting one unit at a time is what makes the smallest scale measurable, so the adjective also describes the data.
senses.whyCN: 逐个单位地数是使最小尺度可测量的方式，因此这个形容词也用来描述这类数据。

senses.title: Naming one branch of economics
senses.titleCN: 作为经济学的一个分支名称
senses.definition: naming the branch of economics that studies single units, as opposed to the branch that studies totals
senses.definitionCN: 命名研究单个单位的经济学分支，与研究对象为总量的分支相对
senses.example: The textbook turns from microeconomic foundations to national accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教材从微观经济的基础转向国民账户。
senses.why: universities divided the subject by the size of its unit, and the adjective became the label of one half.
senses.whyCN: 大学按研究单位的大小划分这门学科，这个形容词便成了其中一半的名称。

senses.title: Applied beyond formal markets
senses.titleCN: 用于正式市场之外的微观分析
senses.definition: describing microeconomic reasoning applied to households, time use and other small-scale choices outside formal markets
senses.definitionCN: 描述把微观经济分析用于住户、时间分配等正式市场之外的小尺度选择
senses.example: Microeconomic reasoning explains how a household divides unpaid work between its members.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济推理可以解释一户人家如何在成员之间分配无偿劳动。
senses.why: the unit of analysis stays the single household or person even when no market transaction is involved, so the adjective travels beyond price-setting.
senses.whyCN: 即使不涉及市场交易，分析单位仍是单户或单人，因此这个形容词能从定价扩展到别的选择。

intro.en: The adjective joins a Greek prefix meaning 'small' to economic, which descends from Greek oikonomikos by way of Latin oeconomicus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把表示「小」的希腊前缀接在 economic 之前，而 economic 经拉丁 oeconomicus 来自希腊 oikonomikos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mikros meant 'small, little'. The reading 'small in scale' is generally thought to be the one that fed the modern prefix.
items.cn: mikros 意为「小的、微小的」。一般认为「尺度上的小」这一读法是现代前缀的来源。

items.en: Oikonomikos described the management of a household, built from oikos 'house' and nemein 'to distribute, manage'.
items.cn: oikonomikos 指家宅的管理，由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「分配、管理」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as oeconomicus, still attached to the estate and the household rather than to a state.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词作 oeconomicus，仍附着于产业与家宅，而非国家。

items.en: English economic, borrowed in the seventeenth century, widened from household management to the wealth and trade of a nation.
items.cn: 英语 economic 于十七世纪借入，从家宅管理扩展到国家的财富与贸易。

items.en: In the twentieth century the combining form for 'small' was attached to economic to mark the scale of a single unit.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，表示「小」的构词成分被接在 economic 之前，以标出单个单位的尺度。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the adjective is generally dated to the mid twentieth century, when analysis of single units was formally named, but no precise first citation is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：一般认为这个形容词在二十世纪中期定名，与微观分析的制度化同步，但确切的首次书证尚未确立。

note.en: Group one lists words that share the same prefix but concern lenses, circuits or worlds; group two lists terms that stand close in meaning or form the opposite scale.
note.cn: 第一组是同用这个表示「小」的前缀、却分别关于透镜、电路与世界的词；第二组是语义相近或构成相反尺度的说法。

entries.definition: The same prefix plus Greek skopein 'to look': too small to be seen without a lens, a term of optics and biology rather than of money.
entries.definitionCN: 同一前缀加希腊语「看」：小到不借助透镜就看不见，属光学与生物学术语，与经济无关。

entries.definition: The prefix plus electronic: belonging to circuits and devices built on a very small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀加「电子的」：属于以极小尺度制造的电路与器件。

entries.definition: The prefix plus Greek kosmos 'world': a small world that mirrors a larger one, with no economic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀加希腊语「世界」：映照大世界的小世界，没有经济含义。

entries.definition: The same economic base with the prefix for 'large': it studies national totals, the exact mirror of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的经济词干配表示「大」的前缀：研究全国总量，正是本词的反面。

entries.definition: From Latin pars 'part': in economics it describes analysis that examines one relation while holding the rest fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pars「部分」：在经济学中描述只考察一重关系、把其余条件保持不变的分析方式。

entries.definition: A transparent compound meaning 'at the scale of an individual company'; it states the unit without the technical label.
entries.definitionCN: 一个意思透明的复合词，指「以单个公司为尺度」；它朴素地说明单位，不带技术标签。

entries.definition: From dis- 'apart' plus grex 'flock': separated from a total into its individual units, the typical form of data used here.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语中表示「分开」的前缀加 grex「群」：从总量拆回各个单位，正是这类研究常用数据的形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix for 'small' plus 'of the economy' gives a word for the economy seen one unit at a time.
normal.cn: 表示「小」的前缀加上「经济的」，得到的是把经济拆到单个单位来看的词。

normal.en: The family runs microeconomic, microeconomics, microeconomist, microeconometric.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microeconomic、microeconomics、microeconomist、microeconometric。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: microeconomic theory, microeconomic analysis, microeconomic reform.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：微观经济理论、微观经济分析、微观经济改革。

normal.en: It forms a pair with macroeconomic: same base, opposite prefix, part versus whole.
normal.cn: 它与 macroeconomic 构成一对：同样的词干，相反的前缀，部分对整体。

normal.en: The phrase microeconomic data usually signals numbers gathered from individual units.
normal.cn: 「微观经济数据」这一搭配通常信号着从各个独立单位收集来的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a single ledger on a shop counter while the street's other shops stay out of frame.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台上摊着一本账，街上其余店铺都留在画面之外。

abstract.en: Picture a biologist adjusting a lens until one cell fills the whole field of view.
abstract.cn: 想象生物学家调着透镜，直到一个细胞占满整个视野。

abstract.en: Picture one stone lifted out of a mosaic so its own colour can be studied.
abstract.cn: 想象从镶嵌画里取出一块石子，好单独研究它自己的颜色。

examples.en: Microeconomic theory predicts how a single seller sets a price.
examples.cn: 微观经济理论预测单个卖方如何定价。

examples.en: The reform was microeconomic in scope, aimed at one industry rather than at national demand.
examples.cn: 这项改革的范围是微观经济的，针对一个行业而非全国需求。

examples.en: Calling a question microeconomic says nothing about how important the answer is.
examples.cn: 把一个问题称为微观经济的，并不说明它的答案有多重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「小」的前缀加「经济的」——把经济拆到一家店、一个柜台来看 → 微观经济的

root: 希腊 mikros「小的」+ oikonomikos（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「分配、管理」）→ 拉丁 oeconomicus → 英语 economic；二十世纪再加表示「小」的前缀，构成指单个主体层面的形容词。首见年份来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses hold one scale steady: a single unit. The line runs from the individual firm or household, to the single market it trades in, to the choices it makes, to the method that isolates one relation, to one industry as a target, to data gathered unit by unit, to the branch label, and finally to everyday choices made outside formal markets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守住同一个尺度：单个单位。这条线从单个企业或住户出发，走向它交易所在的单个市场、它所作的选择、隔离一重关系的方法、作为政策对象的单个行业、逐个单位收集的数据、分支名称，最后落到正式市场之外的日常选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a close-up of one ledger on a counter while the rest of the street stays outside the frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一本账的特写，街上其余一切都被留在画面之外。

branches.en: UNIT AND ARENA: the agent is one firm or household, and the arena where it acts is one market.
branches.cn: 单位与场所：行动的主体是一家企业或一户人家，行动的场所是一个市场。

branches.en: CHOICE AND METHOD: what the unit chooses is studied by isolating a single relation.
branches.cn: 选择与方法：这个单位如何选择，靠隔离一重关系来研究。

branches.en: SECTOR AND DATA: one industry can be regulated, and unit-by-unit records make it measurable.
branches.cn: 行业与数据：单个行业可以被规制，逐个单位的记录又使它可测量。

branches.en: BRANCH LABEL: the scale became the name of one half of the discipline.
branches.cn: 分支名称：这一尺度成了一门学科其中一半的名字。

branches.en: EVERYDAY CHOICE: unit-level reasoning also covers households and time use outside formal markets.
branches.cn: 日常选择：单位层面的推理也覆盖正式市场之外的住户与时间分配。

intro.en: The word can be read morpheme by morpheme: a Greek prefix for size, a Greek noun for the household, a Greek verb for managing, and an English suffix that turns the stem into an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词可以按语素逐个读出：表示尺度的希腊前缀、指家宅的希腊名词、表示管理的希腊动词，以及把词干变成形容词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek oikonomikos reached English through Latin oeconomicus; the Latin noun oeconomia and the agent noun oeconomus belong to the same estate-management family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 oikonomikos 经拉丁 oeconomicus 进入英语；拉丁名词 oeconomia 与施事名词 oeconomus 同属家产管理这一词族。

items.example: The prefix sets the scale of one unit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出单个单位的尺度。

items.example: Mikros is generally thought to be the source of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为这个希腊形容词就是该前缀的来源。

items.example: Oikos names the household that is managed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指被管理的那一家人。

items.example: Nemein supplies the idea of managing a store.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供了「管理储备」的意思。

items.example: The Greek adjective joined house to management.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词把家宅与管理连在一起。

items.example: Latin kept the adjective close to the household.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了它贴近家宅的含义。

items.example: English widened the adjective to the wealth of a state.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个形容词扩展到国家财富。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of a noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词词干变成形容词。

items.meaning: of single units in the economy
items.example: The adjective names the single-unit scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指单个单位的尺度。

items.meaning: the study of single firms and markets
items.meaningCN: 研究单个企业与单个市场的学科
items.example: Microeconomics examines one market at a time.
items.exampleCN: 微观经济学一次考察一个市场。

definition_zh: 现实主义；写实主义；务实态度；实在论
definition_en: the attempt to show things as they really are, or the belief that reality exists independently of the mind
core_image: 画家把街角面包店的旧招牌、脏围裙与找零的手一分不差地画下来
scene: 画家在街角支起画架，把面包店的旧招牌与顾客的皱纹一起画进画里。 The painter set up his easel at the corner and recorded the bakery's worn sign and its customers' wrinkles with realism.
sceneCN: 这里指「如实描绘日常生活的写实手法」（第 1 个义项：艺术中的现实主义）；句意为画家在街角支起画架，用写实手法记录旧招牌与顾客的皱纹。可辨识物件：画架、面包店招牌、顾客、皱纹。

forms.label: 复数形式（指多种现实主义）

derivatives.zh: 现实主义者；写实的（由基础词加表示「信奉者」的后缀构成，语义收窄为立场身份）
现实的；写实的（由表示现实主义者的词加表示「与……有关的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）
现实地；写实地（由前一个形容词加构成副词的后缀构成，语义偏移为方式）

senses.title: Art that shows ordinary life
senses.titleCN: 描绘日常生活的现实主义
senses.definition: a nineteenth-century art movement that depicted ordinary people and everyday scenes without idealising them
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪一场描绘普通人和平常场景、不作美化的艺术运动
senses.example: The painter recorded the bakery's worn sign with realism.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用写实手法画下面包店的旧招牌。
senses.why: The word claims that the artwork corresponds to the thing itself. Ordinary life is chosen because it has not been arranged for display.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主张作品与事物本身相对应。选择日常生活，是因为它没有被安排成展示的样子。

senses.title: Literary realism
senses.definition: a style of fiction that presents plausible people, settings and causes without romantic exaggeration
senses.definitionCN: 以可信的人物、环境与因果呈现生活、不作浪漫夸张的小说风格
senses.example: The novel brought realism to the industrial city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把现实主义带进工业城市。
senses.why: Fiction can either flatter life or report it. Realism chooses report, and its plots follow ordinary cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 小说可以美化生活，也可以报道生活。现实主义选择报道，情节遵循日常的因果关系。

senses.title: The quality of being true to life
senses.definition: the degree to which a work or account matches how things actually look or happen
senses.definitionCN: 作品或叙述与实际外观或实际发生相符的程度
senses.example: The film's realism comes from its unpolished streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的真实感来自未经修饰的街道。
senses.why: Here the word is a measure rather than a movement: any detail that matches experience increases realism.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词是一种尺度，而不是一场运动：任何与经验相符的细节都增加真实感。

senses.title: A practical attitude
senses.definition: the habit of accepting facts and limits rather than wishes or ideals
senses.definitionCN: 接受事实与限制、而非愿望或理想的态度
senses.example: The plan was received with realism rather than hope.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划得到的是务实评估，而非乐观期待。
senses.why: Someone who sees things as they are will not promise what cannot be done. The art sense becomes a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 看清事物本相的人不会承诺做不到的事。艺术义由此变成一种性情。

senses.title: Philosophical realism
senses.definition: the view that reality, or universals, exists independently of how minds perceive or describe it
senses.definitionCN: 认为实在或共相独立于心灵感知与描述而存在的观点
senses.example: Realism holds that the mountain exists before anyone climbs it.
senses.exampleCN: 实在论认为山在有人攀登之前就已存在。
senses.why: Philosophy asks whether the world depends on the observer. Realism answers no, and that answer is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 哲学追问世界是否依赖观察者。实在论回答「不」，这个回答正是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Realism in international relations
senses.titleCN: 国际关系中的现实主义
senses.definition: the theory that states act mainly to pursue power and security in an anarchic world
senses.definitionCN: 认为国家在无政府的世界上主要追求权力与安全的理论
senses.example: Realism explains the alliance as a balance of power.
senses.exampleCN: 现实主义把这个联盟解释为权力平衡。
senses.why: Political realism applies the practical attitude to states: it assumes interests, not ideals, drive decisions.
senses.whyCN: 政治现实主义把务实态度用到国家上：它假定驱动决策的是利益，而非理想。

senses.title: Legal realism
senses.definition: the view that law is what courts and officials actually do rather than only what statutes say
senses.definitionCN: 认为法律在于法院与官员实际怎么做、而不只是条文怎么写的主张
senses.example: Legal realism studies how judges really decide cases.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现实主义研究法官实际如何判案。
senses.why: The same move recurs: look at practice rather than at the official description. Law's realism is about what happens in court.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作反复出现：看实践，而不是看官方描述。法学的现实主义关注的是法庭里实际发生的事。

senses.title: Photographic and cinematic realism
senses.definition: the impression that a photograph or film shows events as they occurred, without intervention
senses.definitionCN: 照片或影片呈现事件如同自然发生、未经干预的印象
senses.example: Handheld camera work adds realism to the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 手持摄影给这个场景增添了真实感。
senses.why: A camera seems to record rather than compose, so its images borrow the word for truth even though every frame is chosen.
senses.whyCN: 摄影机看似记录而非构图，因此它的影像借用了表示「真实」的词，尽管每一帧都是被选定的。

senses.title: Socialist realism
senses.definition: the official style required in Soviet art, showing workers and leaders in an idealised revolutionary light
senses.definitionCN: 苏联艺术中被要求采用的官方风格，以理想化的革命光辉表现劳动者与领袖
senses.example: Socialist realism turned factory work into heroic painting.
senses.exampleCN: 社会主义现实主义把工厂劳动变成英雄式绘画。
senses.why: The name is paradoxical: a style called realism by decree idealises its subjects. The word here marks political approval, not accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称本身矛盾：一种被法令规定为现实主义的风格却在美化对象。此处这个词标记的是政治认可，而非准确。

intro.en: Realism is Latin 'thing' plus the Greek suffix for a system or practice. The philosophical use is oldest, while the artistic use dates from the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: realism 由拉丁语表示「事物」的词加上表示体系或做法的希腊后缀构成。哲学用法最古老，艺术用法则始于十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin res meant 'thing, matter, affair'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 拉丁 res 意为「事物、事情、要务」。其更深来源属「来源不确定」，为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Late Latin realis 'of a thing' produced the English adjective real, first in the sense of something that actually exists.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 realis「关于事物的」产生英语形容词 real，最初指确实存在的东西。

items.en: The suffix -ism came through Latin from Greek -ismos, naming a practice, system or doctrine.
items.cn: 表示学说的后缀经拉丁语来自希腊同名后缀，用来命名一种做法、体系或学说。

items.en: In medieval philosophy realism named the view that universals are real; nominalism was its opposite. This use predates the artistic one.
items.cn: 在中世纪哲学中，realism 指认为共相真实存在的观点，唯名论则是其对立面。这一用法早于艺术用法。

items.en: French criticism used réalisme in the nineteenth century for painters and novelists who reported ordinary life, and English followed.
items.cn: 法国批评界在十九世纪用 réalisme 指报道日常生活的画家与小说家，英语随后跟进。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of res is unresolved, and older Indo-European forms offered for it are reconstructed forms rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：res 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的更早印欧语形式属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same stem that are constantly confused; group two holds competing ways of describing truth to life.
note.cn: 第一组是同出一个词干、极易混淆的词；第二组是描述「贴近生活」的几种竞争性说法。

entries.definition: a person who holds the view, or an adjective describing that style; realism is the view itself.
entries.definitionCN: 持这种观点的人，或描述这种风格的形容词；realism 是观点本身。

entries.definition: sensible and true to life; it describes things, while realism names a movement or doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 合理且贴近现实的；它描述事物，而 realism 指运动或学说。

entries.definition: what actually exists; realism is the attitude or style that respects it.
entries.definitionCN: 实际存在的事物；realism 是尊重它的态度或风格。

entries.definition: land and buildings as property; it comes from real in the legal sense of immovable property, not from realism.
entries.definitionCN: 作为财产的土地与建筑；它来自 real 表示「不动产」的法律义，与 realism 无关。

entries.definition: a style that applies an almost scientific observation of cause and environment; it is stricter and often darker than realism.
entries.definitionCN: 近乎科学地观察因果与环境的一种风格；比现实主义更严格，也常更阴暗。

entries.definition: the deliberate choice of ugly or ordinary detail for maximum accuracy; it pushes realism to an extreme.
entries.definitionCN: 刻意选择丑陋或平常的细节以求最大准确；把现实主义推到极端。

entries.definition: the doctrine that the worth of an idea lies in its practical results; it shares realism's practical temper but is a philosophy of action.
entries.definitionCN: 认为观念的价值在于实际结果的主张；与现实主义共享务实气质，但它是行动哲学。

entries.definition: the view that reality is mental, or the habit of measuring life against ideals; it is the standing opposite of realism in both art and philosophy.
entries.definitionCN: 认为实在是精神的，或以理想衡量生活的习惯；在艺术与哲学中都是现实主义的对立面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Realism is real plus -ism: the doctrine or practice of the thing itself.
normal.cn: realism 是在 real 之后加表示学说的后缀：关于事物本身的做法或学说。

normal.en: The philosophical sense is older than the artistic one, which is why the word also means a belief about reality.
normal.cn: 哲学义比艺术义更古老，所以这个词也指一种关于实在的信念。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its branches: literary, socialist, magical, political.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的分支：文学的、社会主义的、魔幻的、政治的。

normal.en: A realist is the person; realistic is the adjective; realism is the position.
normal.cn: realist 指人；realistic 是形容词；realism 是立场。

normal.en: The stem res means 'thing', so realism always turns attention back to things.
normal.cn: 词干 res 意为「事物」，所以 realism 总是把注意力转回事物本身。

abstract.en: Picture a painter refusing to move a chair because the room looks better without it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家拒绝挪动椅子，因为房间没有它更好看。

abstract.en: Picture a mountain that keeps existing when nobody is looking at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山，在无人观看时仍然存在。

abstract.en: Picture a style ordered by the state to call itself truthful.
abstract.cn: 想象一种被国家要求自称真实的风格。

examples.en: Realism in painting began with scenes of work and poverty.
examples.cn: 绘画中的现实主义从劳动与贫困的场景开始。

examples.en: The report was written with realism about the budget.
examples.cn: 这份报告对预算作了务实的评估。

examples.en: Philosophical realism defends a world independent of our descriptions.
examples.cn: 哲学实在论捍卫一个独立于我们描述的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「真实 + 主义」—— 坚持照着事物本来的样子写和画 → 现实主义、写实主义

root: 由晚期拉丁 realis「关于事物的」加希腊系的学说后缀构成；realis 出自拉丁 res「事物」。res 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，更早的印欧语形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one demand: look at the thing itself. Art, fiction, photography and law apply it to seeing and recording, while practical life, philosophy and politics apply it to belief and decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个要求展开：看事物本身。艺术、小说、摄影与法律把它用于观看与记录，务实生活、哲学与政治则把它用于信念与决策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand recording exactly what is on the table, including the dirt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把桌上的东西原样记下，连灰尘也不漏。

branches.en: ART AND FICTION: painting and the novel report ordinary life instead of improving it.
branches.cn: 艺术与小说：绘画与小说报道日常生活，而不是美化它。

branches.en: MEASURE OF TRUTH: a detail or a camera image can be judged by how closely it matches experience.
branches.cn: 真实尺度：细节或摄影影像可按其与经验的接近程度来评判。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the same demand becomes a practical attitude toward limits.
branches.cn: 性情：同一个要求变成面对限制时的务实态度。

branches.en: TWO POLES: philosophy asserts an independent world, while socialist realism shows a doctrine using the word for approval.
branches.cn: 两极：哲学主张独立世界，社会主义现实主义则展示一种学说如何借这个词表示认可。

branches.en: PRACTICE OVER THEORY: politics and law study what actors actually do.
branches.cn: 实践重于理论：政治与法学研究行动者实际做了什么。

intro.en: Realism is one branch of the large real- family, built on a Latin word for 'thing' and expanded by a suffix for doctrines.
intro.cn: realism 是庞大的 real- 词族中的一支，其核心是拉丁语表示「事物」的词，再由表示学说的后缀扩展而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin res 'thing' gives realis and realitas; English builds real, reality, realize, realism, realist and realistic on that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 res「事物」给出 realis 与 realitas；英语在这一词干上构成 real、reality、realize、realism、realist 与 realistic。

items.example: Res is the stem behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: res 是整个词族背后的词干。

items.example: Realis produced English real.
items.exampleCN: realis 产生英语 real。

items.example: The real chair stood in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 那把真椅子就放在角落里。

items.example: Realism names a doctrine about things.
items.exampleCN: realism 命名一种关于事物的学说。

items.meaning: the doctrine or style of things as they are
items.meaningCN: 照事物本相的主张或风格
items.example: Realism dominated the gallery.
items.exampleCN: 现实主义占据了画廊。

items.meaning: a believer in or maker of realism
items.meaningCN: 现实主义者；写实创作者
items.example: The realist chose a factory gate.
items.exampleCN: 这位写实画家选择了工厂大门。

items.example: The estimate was realistic.
items.exampleCN: 这个估算是合乎实际的。

items.example: Reality resisted the plan.
items.exampleCN: 现实让计划受挫。

items.example: They realized the design in stone.
items.exampleCN: 他们用石头实现了这个设计。

items.example: The light made the street unreal.
items.exampleCN: 那种光让街道显得不真实。

definition_zh: adj. 不对称的（两侧形状不同）；（关系、信息、力量）不对等的
definition_en: Having two halves that differ in shape or size; of a relationship, unevenly balanced in information, power or obligation.
core_image: 一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉
scene: 这件外套左右长短不同，是刻意剪成这样的。 The coat has an asymmetric cut, longer on one side.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asymmetric 指两侧形状或大小不同，即不对称。

pos.zh: 不对称的；不对等的

senses.title: Unequal in shape
senses.definition: having sides or halves that do not match in shape, size or placement
senses.definitionCN: 两侧或两半在形状、大小或位置上不相配
senses.example: The facade is deliberately asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 这个立面是故意做成不对称的。
senses.why: The root means measure, and the prefix removes it, so the word says the two sides cannot be measured alike.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「量度」，前缀把它取消，所以这个词说的是两侧无法用同一尺度量出相同结果。

senses.title: Unequal in a relationship
senses.definition: of information, power or duty, distributed unevenly between the parties involved
senses.definitionCN: 指信息、权力或义务在各方之间分布不均
senses.example: The market fails when information is asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 信息不对称时市场就会失灵。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the shape word for balance, because a lopsided scale is the oldest picture of unfairness.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个形状词来讲「均衡」，因为一头下沉的天平是关于不公最古老的画面。

intro.en: Asymmetric is Greek asymmetros, from a-, without, and symmetria, from syn-, together, and metron, measure: not measuring together.
intro.cn: asymmetric 就是希腊语 asymmetros，由 a-「无」与 symmetria 构成，后者出自 syn-「共同」加 metron「量度」：不能共同量出同一结果。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure lies behind metre, measure and geometry alike.
items.cn: 一个意为「量」的拟构词根同时藏在 metre、measure 与 geometry 背后。

items.en: Greek metron meant a measure or a rule for measuring, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为「量度、量尺」，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: With syn-, together, symmetria meant measuring together, hence proportion and balanced form.
items.cn: 加上 syn-「共同」后，symmetria 意为「共同量度」，因而指比例与匀称。

items.en: The prefix a- negated it, giving asymmetros, without common measure.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 加以否定，得到 asymmetros「没有共同量度」。

items.en: English formed asymmetric in the eighteenth century as geometry and design demanded the term.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪构成 asymmetric，因为几何与设计需要这个术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century economics and strategy applied it to information and power, giving the second sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪经济学与战略学把它用于信息与权力，产生第二个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the whole measure family with and without the negative prefix; the near-meaning group lists everyday words for lopsidedness.
note.cn: 形近组是带与不带否定前缀的整个「量度」词族；近义组列出日常表示「一边偏」的词。

entries.definition: Having matching halves.
entries.definitionCN: 两半相配的。

entries.definition: The absence of symmetry.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏对称。

entries.definition: Relating to shapes and their measures.
entries.definitionCN: 与形状及其量度有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to measurement or a system of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与测量或度量制有关的。

entries.definition: Heavier or lower on one side.
entries.definitionCN: 一侧更重或更低。

entries.definition: Not level, smooth or balanced.
entries.definitionCN: 不平、不匀或不均衡。

entries.definition: Lacking equal weight or stability.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏均等的分量或稳定。

entries.definition: Favouring one side only.
entries.definitionCN: 只偏向一方。

normalIntro.en: Asymmetric is a-, not, plus sym-, together, plus metric, measure: the two sides do not measure the same.
normalIntro.cn: asymmetric 就是 a-「不」加 sym-「共同」加 metric「量度」：两侧量不出同一个结果。

normal.en: Asymmetric and asymmetrical are both correct.
normal.cn: asymmetric 与 asymmetrical 都对。

normal.en: Asymmetry is the noun, asymmetrically the adverb.
normal.cn: asymmetry 是名词，asymmetrically 是副词。

normal.en: Symmetric is the same word without the negative.
normal.cn: symmetric 就是去掉否定的同一个词。

normal.en: Asymmetric information is a set economics phrase.
normal.cn: asymmetric information 是经济学固定说法。

normal.en: Lopsided is the everyday substitute.
normal.cn: lopsided 是日常替换词。

abstract.en: Picture a coat longer on the left than the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一件左边比右边长的外套。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale with one pan clearly lower.
abstract.cn: 想象一头明显下沉的天平。

abstract.en: Think of one side knowing what the other cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一方知道另一方无从知道的事。

examples.en: The garden follows an asymmetric plan.
examples.cn: 这座花园采用不对称的布局。

examples.en: Asymmetric power breeds resentment.
examples.cn: 权力不对等会滋生怨恨。

examples.en: Her smile was slightly asymmetric.
examples.cn: 她的笑略微不对称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「不」+ sym「共同」+ metric「量度」——两边量不到一块儿，就是不对称 asymmetric。

root: 希腊语 metron「量度」加 syn-「共同」构成 symmetria「匀称」，再加否定前缀 a- 成 asymmetros；英语十八世纪造 asymmetric，二十世纪扩用于信息与权力。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses deny a common measure: two halves that will not match, and two parties who do not hold the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都否认「共同量度」：无法相配的两半，以及分量不同的两方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side longer, one pan of the scale clearly lower
core.cn: 核心意象：一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉

branches.en: A coat longer on one side.
branches.cn: 一侧更长的外套。

branches.en: A facade built off centre.
branches.cn: 偏离中线建造的立面。

branches.en: One pan of the scale lower.
branches.cn: 一头下沉的天平。

branches.en: One side knowing more than the other.
branches.cn: 一方比另一方知道得更多。

branches.en: No common measure between the two sides.
branches.cn: 两侧之间没有共同的量度。
