definition_zh: 技术进步；技术能力、工具与工艺水平的提升
definition_en: the improvement of tools, machines, methods or technical knowledge over time
core_image: 同一块田里，牛犁、拖拉机与巡田无人机依次出现，每一代都在同一片土上留下更深的痕迹
scene: 同一块田里，先是用牛拉犁，后来用拖拉机，如今用无人机巡田。 Technological advancement has changed what a single farmer can do in a day.
sceneCN: 这里 technological advancement 指「工具与工艺水平的整体提升」（第 1 个义项：技术能力随时间的进步）；句意为技术进步改变了一个农民一天能完成的工作。可辨识物件：牛犁、拖拉机、无人机、田垄、传感器。

pos.zh: 技术进步（常作不可数）
一项技术进展（可数）

senses.title: General improvement of technique
senses.definition: the broad improvement of tools, methods and technical knowledge over time
senses.definitionCN: 工具、方法与技术知识随时间的广泛改进
senses.example: Technological advancement has changed what a single farmer can do in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 技术进步改变了一个农民一天能完成的工作。
senses.why: Advancement is forward movement, and technology is organised craft; together they name a society's growing capacity to do things.
senses.whyCN: advancement 是向前移动，technology 是组织化的技艺；合起来指一个社会做事能力的增长。

senses.title: A single breakthrough
senses.definition: one major new device or method that opens new possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 一项开辟新可能的重大新装置或方法
senses.example: The vaccine was hailed as a technological advancement of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗被誉为这十年的一项技术突破。
senses.why: The phrase can count individual breakthroughs, not only a long trend, because progress often arrives in steps.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以数出单项突破，而不只是长期趋势，因为进步常以台阶形式到来。

senses.title: Productivity gains
senses.definition: the ability to produce more or better output with the same effort
senses.definitionCN: 以同样投入产出更多或更好的能力
senses.example: Technological advancement in weaving cut the cost of cloth for ordinary households.
senses.exampleCN: 织造技术的进步降低了普通家庭的布料成本。
senses.why: The economic face of the phrase is productivity: new tools change how much one hour of work can make.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的经济面是生产率：新工具改变一小时劳动能造出多少东西。

senses.title: Social change driven by technology
senses.definition: changes in work, communication and daily life that follow new technology
senses.definitionCN: 随新技术而来的工作、通信与日常生活变化
senses.example: Technological advancement reshaped where people could work and whom they could reach.
senses.exampleCN: 技术进步重塑了人们能在哪里工作、能联系到谁。
senses.why: Tools do not stay in the workshop; they rearrange schedules, cities and families.
senses.whyCN: 工具不会留在工坊里；它们重排时间表、城市与家庭。

senses.title: The digital and information leap
senses.definition: the rapid gain in computing, storage and communication capacity
senses.definitionCN: 计算、存储与通信能力的快速提升
senses.example: Technological advancement in chips made a phone more powerful than an old room of computers.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片技术的进步让一部手机比过去一屋子电脑更强。
senses.why: The modern sense is often narrowed to digital gains, because computing has been the fastest-moving frontier.
senses.whyCN: 现代义常被收窄到数字领域的增益，因为计算是最快移动的前沿。

senses.title: Medical and life-science progress
senses.titleCN: 医学与生命科学的进步
senses.definition: new tools for diagnosis, treatment and the understanding of life
senses.definitionCN: 用于诊断、治疗与理解生命的新工具
senses.example: Technological advancement in imaging let doctors see what surgery once had to reveal.
senses.exampleCN: 成像技术的进步让医生看见过去只能靠手术揭示的东西。
senses.why: Where the object is the body, advancement is measured in survival and comfort, not only speed.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是身体时，进步以存活与舒适衡量，而不只是速度。

senses.title: Military and engineering progress
senses.titleCN: 军事与工程技术的进步
senses.definition: gains in materials, propulsion, construction and systems of control
senses.definitionCN: 材料、推进、建造与控制系统的增益
senses.example: Technological advancement in materials made the bridge both lighter and stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 材料技术的进步让这座桥更轻也更坚固。
senses.why: Engineering and warfare have often driven technique forward, because both reward precision and power.
senses.whyCN: 工程与战争常推动技艺前进，因为两者都奖赏精确与力量。

senses.title: Costs and unequal gains
senses.definition: the displacement, inequality and risk that can accompany technical progress
senses.definitionCN: 技术进展可能伴随的取代、不平等与风险
senses.example: Critics ask who bears the costs of technological advancement and who collects its gains.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者追问谁承担技术进步的代价，谁收取它的收益。
senses.why: The phrase is usually positive, but the same tools that raise output can put people out of work, so the sense carries a shadow.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语通常带正面色彩，但提高产出的同一批工具也可能让人失业，因此这一义项带着阴影。

intro.en: Technological joins Greek tekhnē 'art, craft, skill' with -logia 'study', and advancement joins advance, from Old French avancier and Vulgar Latin abantiare, with the noun suffix -ment. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: technological 由希腊 tekhnē「技艺、手艺」加表示「学问」的后缀构成；advancement 由 advance 加名词后缀构成，advance 经古法语 avancier 来自俗拉丁 abantiare。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tekhnē meant 'art, craft, skill, a systematic way of making'. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: tekhnē 意为「技艺、手艺、技能、系统的制作方式」。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Logia meant 'study, discourse' and came from logos 'word, reason'; the compound tekhnologia named a systematic treatment of an art.
items.cn: logia 意为「学问、论述」，来自 logos「言词、理性」；合成词 tekhnologia 指对某门技艺的系统论述。

items.en: English technology appeared in the seventeenth century as a term for the systematic study of arts, and later shifted to the tools themselves.
items.cn: 英语 technology 在十七世纪出现，指对技艺的系统研究，后转指工具本身。

items.en: Advance came through Old French from Vulgar Latin abantiare, built on Latin abante 'from before', from ab 'from' and ante 'before'.
items.cn: advance 经古法语来自俗拉丁 abantiare，源于拉丁 abante「从前方」，由 ab「从」与 ante「前」构成。

items.en: The noun advancement appeared in the fourteenth century, naming a moving forward and then a improvement in rank or knowledge.
items.cn: 名词 advancement 在十四世纪出现，先指向前移动，后指地位或知识的提升。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the combined phrase is not fixed, and the deeper origin of tekhnē is unsettled, so any older form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个组合短语的最早书证无法确定；tekhnē 的更早来源亦无定论，凡更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the two stems; group two names progress in other registers.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词干；第二组是用其他语域表达进步的说法。

entries.definition: The tools and systems themselves; the phrase names their improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 指工具与系统本身；短语指它们的改进。

entries.definition: Relating to technique or machinery, often in contrast to human or artistic matters.
entries.definitionCN: 与技巧或机械相关，常与人或艺术事务相对。

entries.definition: A specific way of doing something; advancement is the gain across many techniques.
entries.definitionCN: 指做某事的具体方法；进步则指许多技巧的整体增益。

entries.definition: Means by means of technology; it does not name progress.
entries.definitionCN: 意为在技术上；不指进步本身。

entries.definition: A broad word for improvement in any field; it does not specify tools.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何领域的改善，不特指工具。

entries.definition: The introduction of new products or methods; one engine of technological advancement.
entries.definitionCN: 指新产品或新方法的引入，是技术进步的一台引擎。

entries.definition: A single decisive advance that removes an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次决定性的进展，消除了障碍。

entries.definition: A wider social process that includes technology but also institutions and habits.
entries.definitionCN: 指更广的社会过程，包含技术，也包含制度与习惯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real contrasts, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实对比，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek word for craft plus the Greek word for study gives the technology half; the Latin word for forward gives the advancement half.
normal.cn: 「技艺」加「学问」组成技术这一半；「向前」加名词后缀组成进步这一半。

normal.en: The family runs technology, technological, technologically, advance, advanced, advancement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 technology、technological、technologically、advance、advanced、advancement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rapid technological advancement, the pace of technological advancement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：迅速的技术进步、技术进步的速度。

normal.en: The phrase can be uncountable for a trend or countable for a single breakthrough.
normal.cn: 这个短语可不可数指趋势，也可可数指单项突破。

normal.en: Remember the cost side: the same tools can raise output and displace workers.
normal.cn: 记住代价面：同一批工具既能提高产出，也能取代工人。

abstract.en: Picture a field where a plough, a tractor and a drone appear in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田里依次出现犁、拖拉机与无人机。

abstract.en: Picture a phone doing the work of a room full of old machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机干完一屋子旧机器的活。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that grows lighter as its metal grows stronger.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥随金属变强而变轻。

examples.en: Technological advancement lowered the cost of solar power faster than forecasts expected.
examples.cn: 技术进步使太阳能成本下降得比预测更快。

examples.en: The report links technological advancement to wage gaps rather than to overall growth alone.
examples.cn: 报告把技术进步与工资差距联系起来，而非只看总体增长。

examples.en: Each technological advancement in printing made books cheaper to own.
examples.cn: 印刷术的每一次技术进步都让书籍更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「technological（技术的）+ advancement（前进）」——工具一代代往前走，把人的手越伸越长

root: technological 来自希腊 tekhnē「技艺」与表示「学问」的后缀；advancement 来自 advance 加名词后缀，advance 经古法语 avancier 出自俗拉丁 abantiare，源于拉丁 abante（ab + ante，从前方）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising line: technique improves overall, a breakthrough opens a door, output rises, society rearranges, computing leaps, medicine and engineering gain, and the costs appear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条上升线展开：技艺整体提高，一项突破打开一扇门，产出上升，社会重新排布，计算能力跃迁，医学与工程获益，代价也随之出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same field crossed first by a plough, then a tractor, then a drone.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块田先被犁走过，再被拖拉机走过，最后被无人机掠过。

branches.en: THE TREND: improvement is continuous and cumulative.
branches.cn: 趋势：改进是连续且累积的。

branches.en: STEPS AND SYSTEMS: a single breakthrough and a whole engineering field both move the line.
branches.cn: 台阶与系统：单项突破与整个工程领域都在推动这条线。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND LIFE: productivity changes work, and work rearranges society.
branches.cn: 产出与生活：生产率改变工作，工作又重排社会。

branches.en: COMPUTING AND BODY: chips and medicine are the two most visible frontiers.
branches.cn: 计算与身体：芯片与医学是最可见的两个前沿。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: every gain has a bearer of cost.
branches.cn: 阴影：每一项收益都有承担代价的人。

intro.en: The phrase can be read from a Greek noun for craft, a Greek noun for study, and a Latin-derived verb of moving forward.
intro.cn: 这个短语可以按表示技艺的希腊名词、表示学问的希腊名词，以及拉丁来源的「向前移动」动词读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek tekhnē supplies technology and technique; Greek logos supplies the study suffix; Latin abante supplies advance and advancement.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 tekhnē 衍生 technology 与 technique；希腊 logos 提供表示学问的后缀；拉丁 abante 衍生 advance 与 advancement。

items.example: The noun supplies the craft half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供词中「技艺」的一半。

items.example: The suffix names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指一个研究领域。

items.meaning: the study of arts; later tools and systems
items.meaningCN: 技艺研究；后指工具与系统
items.example: Technology shifted from study to hardware.
items.exampleCN: technology 从研究转向硬件。

items.example: Technological change is fast.
items.exampleCN: 技术变化很快。

items.example: A technique is one method.
items.exampleCN: 技巧是一种方法。

items.example: The preposition begins the Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个介词开启拉丁短语。

items.example: The word names what stands before.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指在前之物。

items.example: The adverb gave the verb of moving forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词衍生出向前移动的动词。

items.example: Tools advance year by year.
items.exampleCN: 工具逐年推进。

items.example: Advancement can be measured.
items.exampleCN: 进步可以被衡量。

definition_zh: 因果关系；因果作用；引起；归因
definition_en: the relationship between a cause and its effect, or the act of causing something
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌：第一张倒下，第二张跟着倒下，那条传递下去的连接就是因果
scene: 研讨课上，老师把两张图表并排投影：一张显示相关，一张显示因果。他说： Correlation is not causation.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 causation 是「因果关系」（第 1、7 个义项：因果关联与统计中的因果判断）；句意：相关不等于因果。图中可辨识物件：两张折线图、投影仪、粉笔、讲台。

pos.zh: 因果关系；因果作用；引起

forms.label: 复数（多种因果作用，较少用）

senses.title: The relation between cause and effect
senses.definition: the relation in which one event or state brings about another
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件或状态引起另一个事件或状态的关系
senses.example: The study examines the causation of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究考察移民的因果关系。
senses.why: Causation names the link itself, not the cause and not the effect. The word is the bridge between two events, which is why it is so often paired with chain.
senses.whyCN: causation 命名的是连接本身，而不是原因或结果。这个词是两个事件之间的桥，因此常与 chain 搭配。

senses.title: The act of causing something
senses.definition: the action by which something is produced or brought about
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物产生或被造成的行为
senses.example: The report traces the causation of the accident to a faulty valve.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把事故的起因追溯到一个故障阀门。
senses.why: Here the noun names an activity rather than a relation. Someone or something did the causing, and the word points to that doing.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名的是一个活动，而不是一种关系。某人或某物做了“引起”这件事，这个词指向那个作为。

senses.title: Causation as a philosophical principle
senses.titleCN: 作为哲学原理的因果律
senses.definition: the principle that every event has a cause, or that like causes produce like effects
senses.definitionCN: 每个事件都有原因、或相同原因产生相同结果的原则
senses.example: Hume asked whether we can ever observe causation itself.
senses.exampleCN: 休谟追问我们是否真能观察到因果作用本身。
senses.why: Philosophy turned the relation into a principle. What is at stake is not this or that cause, but whether the link is necessary or merely customary.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这种关系变成一条原理。争论的不是某一个原因，而是这条连接是必然的，还是仅仅是习惯性的。

senses.title: Legal causation
senses.definition: in law, the link between a person's act and a result for which they may be held responsible
senses.definitionCN: 法律中某人的行为与其可能须负责的结果之间的连接
senses.example: The court found no legal causation between the warning and the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该警告与伤害之间不存在法律因果关系。
senses.why: Law narrows causation to what is fair to attribute. Not every physical link creates liability; the chain must be close enough to count.
senses.whyCN: 法律把因果收窄到“公平地归责”的范围。并非每条物理连接都产生责任，链条必须足够近才算数。

senses.title: Attributing an outcome to a source
senses.titleCN: 把结果归因于某个来源
senses.definition: the assignment of an observed result to a particular cause or set of causes
senses.definitionCN: 把观察到的结果指派给某个原因或一组原因
senses.example: Attribution of causation requires more than a single case.
senses.exampleCN: 因果归因需要的不只是一个案例。
senses.why: This is causation as a judgement we make, not a fact we see. The word covers the mental move from 'this happened' to 'that made it happen'.
senses.whyCN: 这是作为判断的因果，而不是被看见的事实。这个词覆盖了从“这件事发生了”到“那件事造成了它”的心智移动。

senses.title: A chain or mechanism of causes
senses.definition: a series of linked causes through which an effect is produced
senses.definitionCN: 产生某一结果的一连串相互连接的原因
senses.example: Historians reconstructed the chain of causation behind the famine.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家重建了那场饥荒背后的因果链。
senses.why: Complex outcomes rarely have one cause. The word then refers to the whole mechanism, the set of links that together produce the result.
senses.whyCN: 复杂结果很少只有一个原因。此时这个词指整个机制，也就是共同产生结果的那一组连接。

senses.title: The origins of a disease
senses.definition: in medicine and epidemiology, the factors that bring about a disease
senses.definitionCN: 医学与流行病学中导致疾病的各种因素
senses.example: Researchers still debate the causation of the syndrome.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者仍在争论这种综合征的成因。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word when it needs to separate what brings a condition about from what merely accompanies it. Cause and correlation must be told apart.
senses.whyCN: 医学在需要区分“造成某种状况”与“仅仅伴随它”时使用这个词。原因与相关必须被分开。

senses.title: Causal explanation in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的因果解释
senses.definition: in social research, the attempt to explain social outcomes by identifying their causes
senses.definitionCN: 社会研究中通过确认原因来解释社会结果的尝试
senses.example: The paper argues for multiple causation in urban poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文主张城市贫困存在多因性。
senses.why: Social phenomena have many causes at once, so the word shifts from a single link to a field of interacting factors. The plural causations becomes thinkable.
senses.whyCN: 社会现象同时有许多原因，于是这个词从单一连接转向一组相互作用因素。复数形式 causations 也就变得可想了。

senses.title: Causation versus correlation
senses.definition: the relation that statistical association alone cannot establish
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭统计关联无法确立的那种关系
senses.example: The slogan 'correlation is not causation' warns against hasty inference.
senses.exampleCN: “相关不等于因果”这句口号警告人们不要草率推断。
senses.why: Statistics gave the word its sharpest modern contrast. Two variables can move together without one causing the other, and causation is the name of what is still missing.
senses.whyCN: 统计学给了这个词最尖锐的现代对照。两个变量可以一起变动而互不为因，causation 正是那个仍然缺失的东西的名字。

intro.en: Causation looks like a plain derivative of cause, but it entered English through a Latin noun with a different job. Latin causatio meant 'a pleading, an excuse', and the modern sense 'cause and effect relation' is an English development. This semantic shift is the main thing to notice.
intro.cn: causation 看起来只是 cause 的平实派生词，实际上它是经一个功能不同的拉丁名词进入英语的。拉丁语 causatio 意为“申辩、借口”，而现代“因果关系”义是英语自身的发展。这个语义偏移是此处最该注意的地方。

items.en: Causa meant 'cause, reason, motive', and also 'a judicial case'. English cause and the whole causal family descend from it, not from the unrelated casus 'a fall'.
items.cn: causa 意为“原因、理由、动机”，也指“司法案件”。英语 cause 与整个因果词族都出自它，而不是出自无关的 casus“落下”。

items.en: Causari meant 'to plead, to bring a case, to give as an excuse'. It came from causa in its legal sense, so the verb was about arguing, not about producing effects.
items.cn: causari 意为“申辩、提起诉讼、作为借口提出”。它来自法律义的 causa，因此这个动词讲的是争论，而不是产生结果。

items.en: Causatio, the noun of causari, meant 'a pleading, an excuse, a pretext'. It did not mean the relation between cause and effect, which is the sense English later gave the word.
items.cn: causatio 是 causari 的名词，意为“申辩、借口、托词”。它并不表示因与果的关系，后者是英语后来赋予这个词的意思。

items.en: English adopted causation in the 16th century. Early uses already concerned causing, but the abstract 'cause and effect' sense grew in philosophical writing rather than in law.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪采用 causation。早期用法已涉及“引起”，但抽象的“因与果”义是在哲学写作而非法律中成长起来的。

items.en: Hume and other philosophers made causation a central problem: is the link between events observed, or only inferred from habit? The word became a technical term of epistemology.
items.cn: 休谟等哲学家把因果问题推到中心：事件之间的连接是被观察到的，还是仅由习惯推断出来的？这个词成了认识论的术语。

items.en: Statistics, medicine and law each gave causation a narrower test. The slogan 'correlation is not causation' and the phrase chain of causation belong to the 20th century's effort to separate association from production.
items.cn: 统计学、医学与法律各自给了因果一套更窄的检验。“相关不等于因果”与“因果链”这两个说法，属于 20 世纪把“伴随”与“产生”分开的努力。

note.en: The three words cause, causal and causality sit very close to causation and are often confused. The first group sorts them by part of speech; the second group sorts the neighbouring ideas.
note.cn: cause、causal、causality 与 causation 距离很近，常被混淆。第一组按词性分开，第二组按相邻概念分开。

entries.definition: the principle or property of being causal. Causation is a relation between events; causality is the general capacity or law behind such relations.
entries.definitionCN: 具有因果性的原理或属性。causation 是事件之间的关系，causality 是这种关系背后的普遍能力或规律。

entries.definition: relating to a cause. It is the adjective that modifies links, factors and explanations.
entries.definitionCN: 与原因有关的。它是修饰连接、因素与解释的形容词。

entries.definition: the thing that produces an effect, or to produce one. Cause names one end of the relation; causation names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 产生结果的事物，或产生结果。cause 命名关系的一端，causation 命名关系本身。

entries.definition: a mutual variation of two quantities. It is precisely what causation is often wrongly inferred from.
entries.definitionCN: 两个量之间的相互变化。它正是人们常错误推断出因果的那个东西。

entries.definition: the act of assigning a result to a source. It is the judgement side of causation.
entries.definitionCN: 把结果指派给某个来源的行为。它是因果的判断面。

entries.definition: the process by which something is fixed or decided. It can imply a stronger, more necessary link than causation.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被固定或决定的过程。它可以暗示比 causation 更强、更必然的连接。

entries.definition: the act of bringing something into existence. It stresses the first moment, not the whole causal link.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物开始存在的行为。它强调最初一刻，而不是整条因果连接。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the difference between cause, causation and causality visible, and attach the word to its standard phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩让 cause、causation、causality 的区别保持可见，并把词系到标准搭配上。

normal.en: See the build: cause + -ation, the noun of the process or relation.
normal.cn: 看见构成：cause 加 -ation，表示过程或关系的名词。

normal.en: Say the slogan: correlation is not causation. It fixes the word in its most useful contrast.
normal.cn: 念那句口号：相关不等于因果。它把这个词钉在最常用的对照里。

normal.en: Picture dominoes for chain of causation.
normal.cn: 用多米诺骨牌记 chain of causation。

normal.en: Keep the trio straight: cause is the thing, causal is the adjective, causation is the link.
normal.cn: 把三件套分清：cause 是事物，causal 是形容词，causation 是连接。

normal.en: In law, ask whether the link is close enough to count.
normal.cn: 在法律中，问这条连接是否近到足以算数。

abstract.en: Hold one line between two dots: the line is causation, the dots are cause and effect.
abstract.cn: 抓住两点之间的一条线：线是 causation，两端是原因与结果。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by discipline: philosophy, law, medicine, social science, statistics, everyday attribution.
abstract.cn: 按学科分组义项：哲学、法律、医学、社会科学、统计学、日常归因。

abstract.en: Remember the historical twist: the Latin noun meant 'excuse', not 'cause-effect link'.
abstract.cn: 记住历史转折：这个拉丁名词意为“借口”，不是“因果连接”。

examples.en: The researchers could not establish causation from the survey alone.
examples.cn: 研究者仅凭这项调查无法确立因果关系。

examples.en: Legal causation limits who can be held responsible for a harm.
examples.cn: 法律因果关系限定了谁可以为某项损害负责。

examples.en: Multiple causation is common in complex social problems.
examples.cn: 复杂社会问题中多因性很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“考贼神”：像“考”察案子的“贼”，要把“神”秘的因果链查清——causation 就是因果关系。

root: 拉丁语 causa“原因、理由、诉讼案件”，派生 causari“申辩”与 causatio“申辩、借口”；英语以 cause 加 -ation 构成 causation，并把词义从“申辩”转为“因果关系”。注意它与 casus“落下”无关。

sensesIntro.en: Causation is about a link rather than a thing. Cause names one end, effect names the other, and causation names the connection between them, together with all the questions that connection raises: is it necessary, is it close enough, is it observed or inferred, and is it one link or a whole chain?
sensesIntro.cn: causation 讲的是连接，而不是事物。cause 命名一端，effect 命名另一端，causation 命名它们之间的连接，以及这条连接引出的全部问题：它是否必然、是否足够近、是被观察还是被推断、是一条链还是一整张网。

core.en: The link that carries one event into another: cause at one end, effect at the other.
core.cn: 把一件事带成另一件事的连接：一端是原因，另一端是结果。

branches.en: THE LINK: the relation itself, the act of producing, and whole chains.
branches.cn: 连接：关系本身、产生行为，以及整条链。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: causation as a law of how events work.
branches.cn: 原理：作为事件运行法则的因果。

branches.en: THE LEGAL TEST: a link close enough for responsibility.
branches.cn: 法律检验：近到足以产生责任的连接。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: attributing outcomes, and explaining social ones.
branches.cn: 判断：归因结果，并解释社会结果。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: disease origins and the contrast with mere correlation.
branches.cn: 证据：疾病成因，以及与被单纯相关的对照。

intro.en: Causation is cause plus -ation, and the family keeps the Latin base causa across nouns, adjectives and verbs. The list shows how the same base yields cause, causal, causality and causative.
intro.cn: causation 是 cause 加 -ation，整个词族在名词、形容词、动词中保留拉丁词基 causa。清单展示同一词基如何生出 cause、causal、causality、causative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries include the noun of cause, the verb of pleading, and the noun of pleading. The last two are essential because they explain why English causation looks like a legal word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目包括“原因”名词、“申辩”动词与“申辩”名词。后两者很关键，因为它们解释了为什么英语 causation 看起来像一个法律词。

items.meaning: the cause-effect relation; the act of causing
items.example: Causation is hard to prove from correlation.
items.exampleCN: 仅凭相关很难证明因果。

items.meaning: the source of an effect; a purpose or case
items.example: The cause of the fire was electrical.
items.exampleCN: 火灾的起因是电路问题。

items.example: There is a causal link between the two events.
items.exampleCN: 两个事件之间存在因果联系。

items.meaning: the principle or property of being causal
items.example: The argument questions causality itself.
items.exampleCN: 这一论证质疑因果性本身。

items.meaning: producing an effect; in grammar, expressing cause
items.example: The verb is used in a causative construction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于使役结构。

items.meaning: in terms of cause and effect
items.example: The two factors are causally connected.
items.exampleCN: 这两个因素有因果联系。

items.example: They feared a causeless panic.
items.exampleCN: 他们担心一场无缘由的恐慌。

items.example: He left because the room was too hot.
items.exampleCN: 他离开是因为房间太热。

items.example: The causal chain runs from policy to outcome.
items.exampleCN: 因果链从政策延伸到结果。

items.meaning: a condition that contributes to an outcome
items.example: Smoking is a causal factor in the disease.
items.exampleCN: 吸烟是这种疾病的一个致因因素。

definition_zh: n. 集中化；中央集权化（英式拼写）
definition_en: the act of bringing power, control or activity under one centre; the British spelling
core_image: 所有箭头都从四面八方汇向一个点
scene: 政府把审批权收归一个部门，完成了彻底的集中化。 The government moved all approvals into one department, a complete centralisation.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centralisation 指集中化；句意是政府把审批权收归一个部门。

pos.zh: 集中化；中央集权化

senses.title: Bringing things to one centre
senses.definition: the act of gathering control, records or services into a single place
senses.definitionCN: 把控制权、档案或服务集中到一处
senses.example: Centralisation of records cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 档案集中使等候时间缩短。
senses.why: The word is built from centre plus the suffix of process.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 centre 加上表示过程的词缀构成。

senses.title: Political central power
senses.definition: the transfer of political authority from regions to a national centre
senses.definitionCN: 把政治权威从地方转移到国家中心
senses.example: The reform deepened centralisation in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革加深了首都的中央集权。
senses.why: The political sense follows the general one of moving control inward.
senses.whyCN: 政治含义沿用把控制权向内收拢的一般含义。

intro.en: Centralisation builds on Latin centrum, a centre, through central and the verb centralise.
intro.cn: centralisation 经 central 与动词 centralise，建立在拉丁语 centrum（中心）之上。

items.en: Kentron names the sharp point of a compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指圆规的尖点。

items.en: Centrum names the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 指圆的中心。

items.en: English central means of the middle.
items.cn: 十七世纪 central 意为居中的。

items.en: The verb means to bring to one centre.
items.cn: 十九世纪动词意为集中到一处。

items.en: Centralisation names state control from a capital.
items.cn: 十九世纪指由国家首都统一控制。

items.en: The noun covers any gathering of control.
items.cn: 现代泛指任何控制权的集中。

note.en: The look-alike group swaps spelling or ending; the near-meaning group names concentration and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组替换拼写或词尾；近义组列出集中及其反面。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 美式拼写。

entries.definition: To bring under one centre.
entries.definitionCN: 使集中。

entries.definition: The state of being central.
entries.definitionCN: 中心性。

entries.definition: The act of bringing things together.
entries.definitionCN: 集中。

entries.definition: The joining of parts into one.
entries.definitionCN: 合并巩固。

entries.definition: Control held by a central body.
entries.definitionCN: 中央集权制。

normalIntro.en: Every arrow bends toward one point at the middle.
normalIntro.cn: 所有箭头都弯向中央的一点。

normal.en: Centrum means a centre.
normal.cn: centrum 意为中心。

normal.en: Central means of the middle.

normal.en: Centralise means to gather inward.
normal.cn: centralise 意为向内收拢。

abstract.en: Power folding into one hand.

abstract.en: A wheel with a single hub.

examples.en: Centralisation of buying saved the group money.
examples.cn: 集中采购为集团省了钱。

examples.en: Critics feared the centralisation of policing.
examples.cn: 批评者担心警务权被集中。

examples.en: The report traced a slow centralisation of power.
examples.cn: 报告追溯了权力缓慢集中的过程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森戳来贼身」——森林里把东西都戳到中央来，一身集中在一点。

sensesIntro.cn: 日常含义收拢档案与服务，政治含义收拢权威。

definition_zh: 艺术运动；艺术流派
definition_en: an organised trend in which a group of artists share aims and change how art is made
core_image: 一群艺术家在同一份宣言上签名，随后各自用不同材料表达同一种主张
scene: 十九世纪的画家们联合办展，发表宣言，反对学院派的规矩。 A group of painters held their own exhibition and published a manifesto, founding an artistic movement.
sceneCN: 这里指「一群艺术家共同主张所形成的运动」（第 1 个义项：有共同目标的艺术运动）；句意为这群画家自办展览并发表宣言，开创了一个艺术运动。可辨识物件：画布、宣言纸、签名、展厅。

pos.zh: 艺术运动；艺术流派
（某一时期的）艺术潮流

collocations.phrase: the artistic movements of the twentieth century

derivatives.zh: 艺术家（由基础词根加表示「从事者」的后缀构成，语义收窄为职业）
艺术的；有艺术性的（由表示艺术家的词加表示「与……有关的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）
艺术才能；艺术性（由表示艺术家的词加表示「技艺或集合」的后缀构成，语义偏移为能力）
艺术运动（由表示艺术的词与表示「运动」的词缩略复合，省去形容词形式，语义不变而更常用于史论）

senses.title: A trend with shared aims
senses.titleCN: 有共同目标的艺术运动
senses.definition: an organised trend in which many artists pursue the same aims at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多艺术家在同一时期追求相同目标而形成的组织化潮流
senses.example: A group of painters founded an artistic movement in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 一群画家在首都发起了一场艺术运动。
senses.why: The phrase joins the adjective for art to the noun for motion. A movement is not one work but many works moving in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示艺术的形容词接到表示运动的名词上。运动不是一件作品，而是许多作品朝同一方向移动。

senses.title: A manifesto group
senses.titleCN: 以宣言集结的艺术家团体
senses.definition: a group of artists bound by a published statement of principles
senses.definitionCN: 由一份公开的原则声明联结起来的艺术家群体
senses.example: The artistic movement began with a single manifesto.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动始于一份宣言。
senses.why: Modern movements needed a public text to declare what they rejected. The manifesto turns separate artists into a named body.
senses.whyCN: 现代艺术运动需要一份公开文本，宣告自己拒绝什么。宣言把分散的艺术家变成一个有名号的团体。

senses.title: A period style named later
senses.titleCN: 后来被命名的时期风格
senses.definition: a style of a period that critics and historians name after the fact
senses.definitionCN: 由评论家与历史学家在事后命名的某一时期风格
senses.example: The artistic movement was named by a hostile critic.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动是由一位敌意评论家命名的。
senses.why: Many movements did not choose their names. Critics supplied a label, and the label later became a period category.
senses.whyCN: 许多运动的名字并非自己选定。评论家提供了标签，标签后来成为时期分类。

senses.title: An avant-garde challenge
senses.definition: a movement that deliberately breaks with accepted rules and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 有意与既定规则和机构决裂的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement rejected the academy's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动拒绝了学院的规矩。
senses.why: Avant-garde movements define themselves by what they oppose, so conflict with institutions is part of the sense.
senses.whyCN: 前卫运动以自己反对的东西来定义自身，因此与机构的冲突是这个义项的一部分。

senses.title: A single-medium movement
senses.definition: a movement confined to one art, such as painting, sculpture or photography
senses.definitionCN: 局限于一种艺术门类内的运动，如绘画、雕塑或摄影
senses.example: Photography had its own artistic movement in the same decade.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影在同一个十年里也有自己的艺术运动。
senses.why: Each medium has its own technical problems, so movements often form inside one discipline before spreading.
senses.whyCN: 每种媒介都有自己的技术难题，因此运动常先在某一门类内部形成，再向外扩散。

senses.title: A movement across media
senses.definition: a movement that links painting, literature, music and design under one programme
senses.definitionCN: 在一套纲领下把绘画、文学、音乐与设计联结起来的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement reached poetry and music as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动也波及诗歌与音乐。
senses.why: When a movement has a shared theory rather than a shared technique, it can travel from canvas to page to stage.
senses.whyCN: 当一场运动共享的是理论而非技法，它就能从画布走到书页，再走到舞台。

senses.title: A national or regional movement
senses.definition: a movement tied to the identity or politics of a particular country or region
senses.definitionCN: 与某一国家或地区的身份认同或政治相绑定的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement became part of the independence struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动成为独立斗争的一部分。
senses.why: Art can carry a nation's claim to its own language and history, so a movement may be organised around place as much as style.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以承载一个民族对自身语言与历史的主张，因此运动也可能围绕地方而非风格来组织。

senses.title: A reaction against another movement
senses.titleCN: 针对另一场运动的反动
senses.definition: a movement formed chiefly in opposition to an earlier or rival movement
senses.definitionCN: 主要为反对更早或敌对运动而形成的新运动
senses.example: The next artistic movement answered the first one directly.
senses.exampleCN: 下一场艺术运动直接回应了前一场。
senses.why: Movements come in pairs: one sets a rule, the next breaks it. The phrase can therefore name a reaction as easily as an origin.
senses.whyCN: 运动常成对出现：一场立规矩，下一场破规矩。因此这个短语既能命名源头，也能命名反动。

intro.en: Artistic movement joins an adjective built from art with a noun built from a Latin verb meaning 'to move'. Both halves are old borrowings, while the phrase itself is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artistic movement 把由 art 构成的形容词与一个来自拉丁动词「移动」的名词并在一起。两半都是古老借词，短语本身却是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars 'skill, craft' gives art. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars「技艺、手艺」给出 art。其更深来源属「来源不确定」，为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Artist came through French from Latin artista, itself from ars. English added -ic to make artistic in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: artist 经法语来自拉丁 artista，而 artista 又出自 ars。英语在十八世纪加上表示「与……有关的」后缀，构成 artistic。

items.en: Latin movere 'to move' produced motus 'a moving' and movimentum, the source of movement.
items.cn: 拉丁 movere「移动」产生 motus「运动」与 movimentum，后者是 movement 的来源。

items.en: Old French movement carried the noun into English, where it first meant physical motion and later a collective campaign.
items.cn: 古法语 movement 把这个名词带进英语，最初指物理运动，后来指集体行动。

items.en: Artistic movement became a standard term in the nineteenth century, when critics began grouping artists by shared programmes rather than by individual careers.
items.cn: artistic movement 在十九世纪成为标准术语；当时评论家开始按共同纲领、而非个人生涯给艺术家分组。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origins of ars and movere are both unresolved, so older forms offered for either are reconstructed forms rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ars 与 movere 在拉丁语之前的来源都没有定论，因此为两者提出的更早形式都属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the same words with a different scope; group two holds historical terms for grouped art activity.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样几个词构成、范围不同的形式；第二组是表示群体艺术活动的史学术语。

entries.definition: the usual shorter term in art history; it drops the adjective but keeps the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术史中常用的较短说法；省去形容词，意思不变。

entries.definition: relating to art or to artists; alone it describes a quality, not an organised group.
entries.definitionCN: 与艺术或艺术家有关的；单独使用时描述一种性质，而非组织化群体。

entries.definition: the skill of an artist; it names personal ability, while a movement is collective.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家的技艺；它指个人能力，而运动是集体的。

entries.definition: physical motion, or any organised campaign; the full phrase narrows it to art.
entries.definitionCN: 物理运动，或任何组织化行动；完整短语把它收窄到艺术。

entries.definition: a group of artists sharing a style or teaching; it often implies a master and followers rather than a public programme.
entries.definitionCN: 共享风格或师承的艺术家群体；常暗示师徒关系，而非公开纲领。

entries.definition: the recurring visual features of works; a movement may have a style, but style alone does not imply organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 作品中反复出现的视觉特征；运动可以有一种风格，但风格本身不意味组织。

entries.definition: the advanced group that claims to lead; it stresses rejection of tradition more than the phrase artistic movement does.
entries.definitionCN: 自称走在前列的先进群体；比 artistic movement 更强调拒绝传统。

entries.definition: a general direction of change; it can be unplanned, while a movement implies shared intent.
entries.definitionCN: 变化的大方向；可以是无计划的，而运动暗示共同意图。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Artistic is artist plus -ic, so the phrase literally means the art-related movement.
normal.cn: artistic 是在 artist 之后加表示「与……有关的」后缀而成，因此这个短语字面上就是「与艺术有关的运动」。

normal.en: Movement goes back to a Latin verb for moving, which is why a trend can be pictured as many works walking one way.
normal.cn: movement 上溯到拉丁语表示「移动」的动词，所以一场潮流可以想象成许多作品朝同一方向行走。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its stages: found, lead, join, and later study a movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的阶段：创立、领导、加入，后来是研究一场运动。

normal.en: Art movement is the shorter term used most often in textbooks.
normal.cn: art movement 是教科书中最常用的较短说法。

normal.en: Many movements were named by critics, which is why the label sometimes sounds hostile.
normal.cn: 许多运动由评论家命名，这也是标签有时带敌意的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd walking in one direction without a leader visible at the front.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人朝同一方向走，最前面却看不见领队。

abstract.en: Picture a signature page where every name is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签名，每个名字都出自不同的手。

abstract.en: Picture a rule being written down so that the next generation can break it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规矩被写下来，好让下一代去打破它。

examples.en: Impressionism began as an artistic movement with its own exhibitions.
examples.cn: 印象派最初是一场自办展览的艺术运动。

examples.en: The artistic movement spread from painting into poetry and music.
examples.cn: 这场艺术运动从绘画蔓延到诗歌与音乐。

examples.en: Later critics treated the artistic movement as a single period style.
examples.cn: 后来的评论家把这场艺术运动当作一个统一的时期风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艺术的运动」—— 一群艺术家朝同一个方向一起走 → 艺术运动、艺术流派

root: 由 artistic 与 movement 组合：artistic 源于拉丁 ars「技艺」经 artist 加表示「与……有关的」后缀；movement 经古法语上溯至拉丁 movere「移动」及其派生 movimentum。两者的更早来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a collective drift: a shared aim, a manifesto, a later label, an avant-garde break, one medium, many media, a nation, and finally a reaction against the movement before it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次集体转向展开：共同目标、宣言、事后标签、前卫决裂、单一媒介、跨媒介、国族，最后是对前一场运动的反动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many artists walking one way, each carrying a different tool.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多艺术家朝同一方向走，每人手里拿着不同的工具。

branches.en: ORIGIN: a shared aim becomes public when a group writes it down.
branches.cn: 起点：共同目标在群体把它写下来时成为公开纲领。

branches.en: AFTERLIFE: critics turn the group into a period style with a name.
branches.cn: 身后：评论家把这个群体变成一个有名号的时期风格。

branches.en: OPPOSITION: the movement defines itself by what it refuses.
branches.cn: 对抗：运动以自己拒绝的东西来定义自身。

branches.en: MEDIA: one discipline or several can carry the same programme.
branches.cn: 媒介：一门或数门艺术都能承载同一套纲领。

branches.en: PLACE AND REACTION: a national cause and a counter-movement show that art moves with politics and with its rivals.
branches.cn: 地方与反动：民族事业与反向运动说明艺术会随政治与对手一起移动。

intro.en: The phrase is built from art and motion, and both halves bring productive families into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由「艺术」与「运动」构成，两半都为英语带来能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars gives art, artist, artistic and artisan; Latin movere gives move, movement, motion and motive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 给出 art、artist、artistic 与 artisan；拉丁 movere 给出 move、movement、motion 与 motive。

items.example: Ars is the root of art.
items.exampleCN: ars 是 art 的词根。

items.example: Art changed meaning over centuries.
items.exampleCN: art 的含义在几个世纪中发生变化。

items.example: Artist means one who works in art.
items.exampleCN: artist 指从事艺术的人。

items.example: The artist joined the group.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家加入了那个群体。

items.example: Artistic means relating to art.
items.exampleCN: artistic 意为与艺术有关的。

items.example: The artistic aims were new.
items.exampleCN: 这些艺术目标很新。

items.structure: movere, movi, motum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: Movere gives movement and motion.
items.exampleCN: movere 给出 movement 与 motion。

items.structure: Old French movement, from Latin movimentum
items.example: The movement grew quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动发展得很快。

items.example: The artistic movement had a manifesto.
items.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动有一份宣言。

items.example: Art movement is the textbook term.
items.exampleCN: art movement 是教科书的说法。
